texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwg7:
Smoke appears after explosion heard in Iowa near Army detonation site
The US military has hailed as a "huge success" the detonation of nearly five tonnes of toxic explosives in Iowa, an operation that sparked fears of health and environmental problems across the region.
Smoke was seen rising into the sky shortly after 09:00 local time (14:00 GMT) following the explosion, as the Army declared the risk "as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible".
Plans to detonate the lead azide, a volatile compound reportedly at risk of exploding on its own, were paused several times before the blast following public outcry and legal challenges.
On Wednesday evening, the Army said that an "all clear" has been issued around the ammunition plant.
President Donald Trump said shortly after the blast that reports showed mitigation efforts "far exceeded expectations".
"The Army's controlled, mitigated detonation exceeded all expectations and was a HUGE success," Adam Telle, acting secretary of the US Army, wrote on social media.
Despite widespread concern from residents of Middletown, Iowa, ahead of the blast, officials have said that lead readings in the area so far have been promising.
In a Wednesday evening update on X, the Army said that the Federal Emergency Management Agency (Fema) had issued the "all clear" around the plant and that there was no airborne lead detection following the detonation.
"Post-detonation surface sampling is underway, and results will be released once complete," the Army added.
Environmental Protection Agency administrator Lee Zeldin also said on social media that in the hours after the detonation "all EPA air monitors continue to report a ZERO DETECT of airborne lead".
The explosives had been in storage for around 20 years, and degraded as part of a process known as recrystallisation - this made them more responsive to accidental detonation from friction or other movement.
No level of lead exposure is considered safe, with children and pregnant women particularly vulnerable to harmful effects.
Middletown Mayor Rodney Johnson told the BBC he felt "relieved" after the detonation.
He watched the blast from his job at a manufacturing plant eight miles (12km) away from the blast - and monitored a camera at his two-bedroom home just one mile from the detonation site.
"We did not feel anything. We did not see anything," Johnson said.
Also eight miles away from Middletown, Sandy Mabeus closed the windows and the garage at her home, brought their outdoor cat inside and hunkered down.
The family watched three separate live streams on iPads and televisions of the explosion as it happened.
"We did not feel or hear a thing here," she told the BBC, adding that she checked the videos to confirm it had actually happened.
"The waiting and wondering has not been a good thing for anybody in the area," she said. "Hopefully they had a very good result and we can just get on with things."
Iowa farmer David Vandenberg lives about 20 miles from the blast site and said he first learned of the detonation around two weeks ago. The Army Corps of Engineers took samples from his yard and pond on Tuesday.
"I was listening this morning, and I did hear a rumble about nine o'clock," he told the BBC on Wednesday, but didn't see or smell anything.
Vandenberg expects officials to return to take more samples but "was happy to see that the blast was relatively contained. "I think the effects will be minimal"
Illinois Governor JB Pritzker said on X that his state was "seeing little to no impact" from the blast. In a press release, he said he was directing state agencies to remain on standby for any "unanticipated impact".
The Iowa site is only 10 miles (16 km) from the Illinois border.
Iowa's incoming Governor-elect Rob Sand said there was "more testing to do" and called for "immediate transparency" to explain why the lead-up was "so chaotic and unclear".
Sand said that any Iowans who have been impacted in any way "must be taken care of fully, right away".
Cameron Hamilton, the Fema administrator, said there would be additional resources and testing in the coming days and weeks.
In recent weeks, the US Army scheduled and rescheduled their detonation ahead of colder winter temperatures.
It also warned locals of "potential exposure to toxic lead dust", which led to some panic. It instituted measures including an optional evacuation zone and a shelter-in-place advisory ahead of the detonation.
The Army faced pushback from residents and politicians alike and there were legal challenges to prevent the detonation from going ahead on environmental and health grounds.
But on Monday, the appeals court overturned a decision to halt the blast. It said that - while these concerns were valid - the risk from an unplanned explosion was greater.

Hours after detonating 4.4 tons of lead azide in Iowa, officials reported early test results from the surrounding areas.
Saying it was necessary to prevent the possible spontaneous explosion of a stockpile of material used in igniters and blasting caps, the US Army conducted a controlled detonation of over 9,700 pounds of lead azide today at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa. Videos of the detonation showed plumes of smoke several hundred feet high drifting south before quickly dissipating.
Following the explosion, the Army confirmed that all of the barrels at the plant had been destroyed without any secondary explosions or infrastructure damage. “I believe, absolutely, that we reduced, as close to zero as it’s absolutely humanly possible, the risk to the health and safety of the people of Middletown and the extended communities throughout Iowa,” said Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley during a press conference held two hours after the blast, according to the Associated Press .
The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has been monitoring the area around the ammunition plant leading up to today’s event. According to a statement from the EPA following the detonation, “real-time air monitors are reporting zero detection of airborne lead throughout the region” an hour after the detonation. The data collected by EPA employees, contractors, and monitoring equipment is shared here .
The Army has used lead azide in munitions for nearly a century but began transitioning away from the material around 15 years ago because it can be difficult to transport and store. Over time, the material can degrade and crystallize and eventually become unstable enough to detonate at ambient temperatures. The Iowa ammunition plant housed 68 barrels containing about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, representing the country’s remaining stockpile. For safety reasons, the material was stored in liquid form embedded in sawdust and burlap bags while water and ethanol were added to prevent freezing. However, the decision was made to detonate the stockpile after an inspection by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms (ATF) discovered “significant crystallization on the exterior of the barrels” last March.
Ahead of today’s detonation, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) supported a recommended, but voluntary, temporary relocation of all the residents of Middletown and immediate surrounding areas that began yesterday. A cone-shaped evacuation zone extends about five miles southwest of the ammunition plant to account for the post-explosion dispersion and deposition path of dust. Displaced residents will be lodged until Friday, November 27th, and can return home once the all-clear has been given.
To reduce the amount of lead dust released into surrounding areas and the environment, the Army said it took several additional precautions as part of today’s detonation. Walls made of four 16,000-gallon water tanks were installed to capture lead particulate, while the aging earth-covered magazines holding the barrels were covered with tarps and lead containment screens and flooded with foam.

The total value of the shares could reach almost $18bn and comes as tech companies debate how to share the spoils of the AI boom
Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, has pledged to give every child in the US two shares in SpaceX, the space ⁠and AI company he ​runs, worth a total of almost $18bn.
In a brief post on X, the social media platform that he owns, Musk said children will receive one share from the company itself, and one from him personally. SpaceX announced earlier on Wednesday that it would ​contribute one newly issued share of its Class A common stock ‌to every currently active Trump Account, and that ‌Musk will match the number of shares it donates.
The Trump account program was designed to give every American under 18 a stake in the stock market, to help build wealth from an early age. The White House said last month that it had opened almost 70 million accounts. SpaceX shares closed at $127.44 on Wednesday, valuing the pledge at nearly $18bn.
SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether Musk’s own donations would also be linked to Trump accounts.
In a separate post, Musk said the company shares will be transferred next ⁠month, with his own to follow later. “The share directly from me will be transferred when my lockup expires in June next year,” he wrote.
In October, Musk, whose net worth is around $824bn, announced his intention to give one of his SpaceX shares to every child in America. “This will be the first of many,” he said in a post on X at the time. As of June, he held about 6.42bn shares ​in the company.
Most of Musk’s philanthropic efforts have been conducted via the Musk Foundation, which reportedly holds around $16bn in assets.
In October, SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell ⁠and her husband pledged a share of their SpaceX stock to each of more than 2 million children under ​the Trump account initiative.
Musk and rival AI company Anthropic have recently detailed their sharply different approaches for sharing the spoils of the AI boom. Anthropic, which went public earlier this month, ​said it would commit 5% of its ​shares to a new fund for the “public good”. The company said this initiative, worth around $54bn at current prices, would give it ​more flexibility and scale to ‌make donations for the benefit ​of humanity.
Other major, long-running philanthropy ventures include those of Berkshire Hathaway chair emeritus Warren Buffett, who is reported to have given away $60bn, with the intention of doing the same with most of the rest of his $150bn fortune.
The Gates Foundation has distributed more than $100bn since its founding in 2000, with some of that fuelled by donations from Buffett.

Dario Amodei’s remarks come amid predictions AI could soon surpass human intelligence.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has denied believing that humanity should “surrender” control to artificial intelligence amid predictions that models potentially far exceeding human intelligence are imminent.
In a lengthy post on X on Wednesday, Amodei said he does not support surrendering “human free will” to AI and has long argued that the frontier technology should be subject to “legitimate democratic processes”.
“If I thought any of this was a good idea, I would be advocating for it in public, just as I have not been afraid to advocate for many, many unpopular views over the last few years,” Amodei said, responding to an Axios report about a purported “consensus” inside Anthropic that some decision-making authority should be passed to the technology.
“But I am not advocating for it, because I think turning over governance to AI is a terrible idea.”
Amodei’s remarks come amid a flurry of commentary by top industry executives suggesting that AI will soon match or surpass human intelligence.
The prospect of AI that equals or outperforms the best human minds – referred to as artificial general intelligence (AGI) and artificial super-intelligence (ASI), respectively – has fuelled intense debate in Silicon Valley and beyond about whether such technology can be harnessed for good without exposing humanity to catastrophic harm.
AI safety advocates have raised fears that models being developed by firms such as Anthropic, which made history last week in the biggest initial public offering of all time, could slip out of human control, particularly once systems start improving without human input, a process known as recursive self-improvement.
In his X post, Amodei criticised commentary he said conflated the idea of AI taking over specific tasks with surrendering control in a “grand sense of global governance”.
“This is not AI ‘running the world’, but AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing software end-to-end,” Amodei said.
“Here, my view is mixed. AI doing more complete or larger tasks is economically valuable and can drive important advances in software, medicine, transportation, energy, etc.”
“It is clearly desirable in many cases and will save a lot of lives,” he added. “But it has downsides as well, and in some areas it may not be worth it.”
Citing unnamed sources, Axios reported on Wednesday that Amodei and other Anthropic executives believe it would be irrational “or even unethical” not to hand over authority to AI for tasks it can do better than humans, such as curing diseases.
David Krueger, the founder of Evitable, a nonprofit that advocates for a pause on development of ASI, said Anthropic should pause its work if Amodei is genuinely concerned about humanity losing control of frontier models.
“We don’t have to consciously surrender control to AI to lose it. As AI becomes increasingly capable, there will be mounting pressure to push humans out of decision-making roles across society,” Krueger told Al Jazeera.
“Meanwhile, researchers at Dario’s own company are warning that AI capabilities are advancing faster than our ability to control them. We need an immediate, indefinite, international moratorium on frontier AI development.”
While there is no universally agreed-upon definition of AGI or ASI, key tech industry figures have over the past week suggested that the milestones are near.
Google DeepMind’s chief AGI scientist and cofounder, Shane Legg, said on Wednesday he believes there is a more than 50 percent chance that “minimal” AGI arrives before 2028.
On Sunday, Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, said ASI is “arriving” , pointing to the announcement that an Anthropic employee had used Claude to solve the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most difficult problems in mathematics.
“How humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence on what future world we live in,” Wang said on X.

Şifre yönetim hizmeti 1Password, arka uç sistemlerini hedef alan bir siber saldırı yaşandığını duyurdu. Şirketin 25 Kasım Çarşamba günü yaptığı açıklamaya göre inceleme, 19 Kasım'da fark edilen yetkisiz erişim bulgularıyla başladı. Saldırganın bazı müşterilere ait bilgileri kopyaladığını doğrulayan şirket, kullanıcılarını sahte mesaj girişimlerine karşı da uyardı.
1Password'un incelemesine göre saldırgan, bir şirket çalışanının kurumsal GitHub hesabına yetkisiz erişim sağlayarak işe koyuldu. Bu hesap üzerinden kaynak kodlarına ulaşan saldırgan, arka uç hizmetlerine kötü amaçlı kod yükledi ve müşterilere ait yönetim verilerini bu kod aracılığıyla indirdi. Şirket etkilenen GitHub hesabını devre dışı bırakarak saldırganın erişimini engellediğini, açığa çıkmış olabilecek tüm dahili kimlik bilgilerini de yenilediğini veya iptal ettiğini açıkladı.
Saldırıdan müşterilerin bir bölümü etkilendi ve bu kişilere ait isimler, e-posta adresleri ile hesaplarla ilgili gizli olmayan dahili üst veriler kopyalandı. Kopyalanan kayıtlar arasında hesap ve kullanıcı kimlik numaraları, hesapların açılış tarihleri ve son oturum açma zamanları da yer alıyor. Davet ve hesap kurtarma gibi işlemler için e-postayla gönderilen bağlantılardaki bazı doğrulama anahtarları da saldırganın eline geçti.
1Password, saldırganın kullanıcıların şifre kasalarına, kasalarda saklanan bilgilere ve bunları koruyan anahtarlara ulaşamadığını vurguladı. Şirketin anlattığına göre sistem, sunuculara sızılsa bile kasa içeriği açığa çıkmayacak şekilde tasarlandı, çünkü gizli bilgiler yalnızca kullanıcıda bulunan anahtarlarla şifreleniyor. Bu nedenle kullanıcıların 1Password hesaplarında herhangi bir güncelleme yapmasına gerek bulunmuyor.
Ele geçirilen isim ve e-posta adresleri dolandırıcıların sahte güvenlik uyarıları göndermesine zemin hazırlayabileceği için şirket müşterilerinden kimlik avı girişimlerine karşı dikkatli olmalarını istedi. 1Password, kullanıcılardan hesap parolasını veya gizli anahtarını hiçbir zaman talep etmeyeceğini de hatırlattı. Alınan önlemler kapsamında kurtarma e-postalarında kullanılan altı rakamlı kodlar on karaktere çıkarıldı.

At least 30 people were killed and 15 others injured after a fire broke out on a major highway in the Egyptian capital Cairo on Wednesday, the country's Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said.
The blaze erupted after a truck carrying fuel overturned on a busy highway, according to Egyptian state media.
Footage captured by passers-by showed a massive blaze and thick clouds of smoke rising from the scene.
Emergency workers pulled people from burning vehicles as firefighters battled the flames. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a suburb of Cairo.
Abdel Ghaffar said 39 ambulances were dispatched to the scene, with 15 injured people taken to hospital.
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement.
The Health Minister said he would visit the scene, adding that the death toll was preliminary and could rise further.
Traffic accidents claim thousands of lives in Egypt every year, with speeding, poor road conditions and inadequate enforcement of traffic laws among the leading causes of crashes.
In January, 21 people were killed and 16 others injured in a multi-vehicle collision on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.

Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says.
Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening.
Footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched.
Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the tanker had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.
The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead.
The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation.
It then crossed the central reservation, overturned and caught fire, the state-owned newspaper says.
Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years, with informal residential areas and often run-down infrastructure making incidents more common, the response to which is often complicated by slow emergency response times and locally improvised rescue efforts, even in the sprawling Egyptian capital.
Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished, as emergency services blocked off entry routes.
Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished
The tanker crossed the highway's central reservation before overturning and bursting into flames, local media report
The health ministry said 39 ambulances had been dispatched to respond to the fire, while it posted images of Egypt's health minister overseeing the treatment of the injured at one of Cairo's hospitals.
Road collisions are also common in Egypt, often attributed to lax maintenance and the widespread flouting of traffic laws.
Nearly 6,000 people died on Egypt's roads last year, official figures show, a rise of several hundred on the previous year's total.
Emergency responders have since cleared the highway and allowed it to reopen, state broadcaster NMA reports.
A bulldozer could earlier be seen at the scene clearing the burnt-out wrecks of cars.

Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred
A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.
The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.
State media reported that the fire broke out when the fuel truck overturned. The stretch of the highway where it occurred was in Waraq, a densely populated neighbourhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, the health ministry said.
At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video showed firefighters working to put out the fire spreading among the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene.
Ahmed Sameer, who was stuck in traffic as the road was blocked after the accident, saw the fuel truck and many cars on fire. He said he saw at least eight bodies being removed from burned cars.
“It was a huge fire, the cars got stuck together because of the fire,” he said, describing the fear and panic that followed. “It was a shocking scene.”
The Egyptian president, Abdel Fatah al-Sisi, expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. The public prosecutor’s office said DNA investigations were under way to identify the victims.
The health minister, Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and that the death toll was preliminary, raising concerns it could rise further. He later travelled to the scene and to the hospitals, the health ministry said.
The minister’s spokesperson told the state-linked Al-Qahera News that the ring road had been reopened and the remnants of the accident cleared.
Deadly traffic incidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record. Speeding, bad roads and poor enforcement of traffic laws are the main reasons behind most of the crashes.
In January, 21 people were killed and 16 were injured in a multicar pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.

Forecasters say high winds on Thursday may spoil the annual march of huge balloons and have moved the parade to Saturday
New York City’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade has been postponed due to excessively windy weather and will now be held on Saturday.
Forecasters say an impending storm on Thursday may spoil the street party, which is marked by a march of huge balloons. AccuWeather is forecasting winds of 12 to 25 mph (19 to 40 km/h) and rain later on Thursday.
Under guidelines, large balloons must stay grounded if sustained winds exceed 23 mph (37 km/h) or gusts exceed 34 mph (55 km/h). The parade balloons have been grounded only once previously, in 1971.
NBC quoted Macy’s as saying: “The safety of our participants and spectators is our priority.”
Macy’s added: “Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.”
This year the parade will include a tribute to Dolly Parton led by Megan Hilty, and special appearances by Melissa Joan Hart, Jack McBrayer, Janet McTeer and Holly Robinson Peete, all leading the way for Santa Claus. Nine Broadway shows will be featured as part of a 10-minute medley, replacing the traditional sprinkling of full show numbers.
The Macy’s parade began more than a century ago in 1924 as a way of creating buzz for the giant department store’s holiday windows at Macy’s Herald Square flagship store in Manhattan. Macy’s borrowed animals from the Central Park Zoo for the first parades but in 1927 ended that practice after children were getting scared.
The animals were then replaced with air-filled balloons and, a year later, balloons that could be filled with helium – a now familiar sight for people around the world from countless Hollywood movies set in New York City.
The parades have been fully cancelled previously only in 1942, 1943 and 1944 because the valuable materials needed to create the huge balloons were diverted for the the second world war effort against Germany and Japan.

We recently released NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Parse , a compact document model that turns page images into structured data for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agents.
Now we’re building on that release with synthetic training datasets, a fine-tuning recipe, and a DFlash2 speculator for faster inference . We’re also sharing how we trained Parse 3.5: first teaching document understanding through supervised fine-tuning, then using reinforcement learning to improve accuracy, consistency, and reliable completion.
Parse extracts content from pages of documents into reading order, assigns content classes such as headings, paragraphs, tables, and charts, and returns bounding boxes that locate the content. Tables and charts become structured records that can power downstream document processing applications.
Figure 1. Actual model output from a synthetic operations brief, showing the connection between the page and its structured representation.
This latest version of Parse significantly extends its ability to read charts and tables, especially in more difficult and ambiguous cases. For example, bar charts or other plots that do not have any marked numeric values. The model is able to infer values by looking at the axes and height of the bar to derive these. Tables can be especially tricky because the structure is so meaningful, a shifted row or column can totally change the interpretation and meaning. These advancements have been largely powered by synthetic data generation, rendering variations of charts and tables with known ground truth and then training our model to reverse this process.
We are open-sourcing three datasets used in the Parse 3.5 training :
Synthetic Charts V1 — 9.98M examples : rendered charts and structured annotations for learning categories, series, and numerical values.
Synthetic Tables V1 — 1M examples : rendered HTML tables with targets that preserve rows, columns, headers, and cell relationships.
OCR Synthetic Multilingual v2 — 7.9M examples : synthetic document pages with Parse-format targets across varied fonts and layouts, for multilingual OCR and structured page reading.
Each release includes images, annotations, generation documentation, and the training format. Use these pairs to fine-tune document models or create new variations for a target document type or language.
Figure 2. Parse recovers 18, 27, 39, and 54 from the chart geometry
We trained Parse 3.5 with two phases of training. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) spanning text, layout, tables, charts, and multilingual documents. Learning to predict structured targets established the general capability of reading a page and representing its contents.
We then continued with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) , using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) . Rewards check the quality of sampled extractions. For example, a chart extraction can earn a better reward for recovering the correct series and values, producing a usable structure, and finishing without repeatedly generating the same content.
A difficult page can have several valid representations. These checks give the model flexibility to find a correct answer without prescribing one exact token sequence, while discouraging looping and unfinished output.
Figure 3. A controlled comparison of SFT and GRPO with matched evaluation settings. These are development checkpoints, separate from the final released model. Loop counts use a repetition check. Methods .
The matched comparison shows the benefit: loop-flagged outputs fall from 126 to 29 pages—about 77% fewer —and outputs reaching the 9,000-token limit fall from 185 to 35 . Overall score improves from 66.24 to 71.38 , including +5.18 points in tables and +4.15 in charts .
A parser must generate substantial text and structure for every page. Alongside the training work, we optimized how Parse 3.5 processes images and decodes those outputs.
NaViT preprocessing adapts the input shape to the page. A visual adapter compresses the image sequence, and the text decoder consumes it as a prefix, replacing encoder–decoder cross-attention. Grouped-query attention with eight key/value heads (GQA-8) reduces the decoder’s attention-cache memory.
The built-in multi-token prediction (MTP) head supplies one-token lookahead. Our DFlash2 speculator goes further: a small draft model proposes up to 32 tokens ahead , and Parse verifies the proposals together. In the measured 32-token configuration, it averages about 14 accepted draft tokens , or roughly 15 output tokens of progress per verification step including the target token.
Figure 4. Native single-pass throughput on one H200, BF16, using the same 2,078 pages. Parse 2.0 uses one trial per point; Parse 3.5 shows three-trial medians. Arrows show the gain from Parse 3.5 base to DFlash2. Measurement details .
In the native single-pass benchmark on one H200 in BF16, DFlash2 increased throughput 7.62× at concurrency 1 and 1.52× at concurrency 512, compared with Parse 3.5 with speculative decoding disabled. At 512, Parse 3.5 reaches 13.48 pages/s without speculation and 20.44 pages/s with DFlash2, versus 2.98 for Parse 2.0. Those are 4.53× and 6.86× the Parse 2.0 throughput, respectively.
Fast parsing gives us room to revisit difficult regions. Start with a full-page prediction, then add focused reprocessing where the document needs it:
Single pass - Parse the full page once for text, layout, tables, and charts.
Double pass - use for dense tables and small chart details. Crop the table and chart regions found by the parser, re-parse them at higher detail, and merge the refinements into the page output.
Triple pass - Instead of only using the models full page parsing bounding boxes, use a second pass of the model in detection mode in order to get verification that all boxes have been accurately found and text has not been missed and re-extract any found charts or tables in a third pass
Figure 5. Additional stages focus computation on difficult regions. Multiple crops can require multiple requests.
In the published reference evaluation, double and triple pass add 2.18 and 2.46 ParseBench points over single pass. The additional work lets applications trade some throughput for better extraction in difficult regions. Reference results and serving measurements .
We are sharing a Parse fine-tuning recipe that takes developers through paired data generation, NeMo Automodel SFT , and NeMo RL GRPO , using vLLM to generate candidate answers.
The worked example uses a synthetic dental form with an odontogram : a chart showing teeth, planned procedures, and affected tooth surfaces. Before adaptation, Parse reads the printed tooth numbers but misses the intended procedure table. SFT teaches it to associate each marked tooth with a procedure and its placement on the tooth.
Figure 6. A recorded recipe example: after SFT, all six chart rows match the target. Full image and native training label .
RLVR then reinforces accuracy and consistent completion. In the dental reference run, the estimated first-attempt success rate (sampled pass@1) rose from 0.00% for the base model to 95.85% after SFT and 96.58% after RLVR.
Figure 7. Matched evaluation on 256 held-out forms from the same synthetic generator, with eight samples per page. Success requires natural completion, exact chart content, and error-free normalized page text. Evaluation protocol .
To adapt the recipe, supply your own image/label pairs and a verifier: checks that determine whether an extraction is correct. The included document reward components cover text fidelity, bounding boxes, tables, chart facts, and completion. Combine the components relevant to your task, add schema checks, and use completion and repetition checks to discourage looping or unfinished output.
We are excited that the community has extended and improved Parse for Thai , Persian/Farsi , and Arabic already and we hope that these additional datasets and fine-tuning recipes will help encourage these efforts a…

New York City mayor on postponing 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade
Macy's has postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to Saturday because of severe weather.
Preparations to hold the iconic holiday celebration, known for its massive balloons that float among the city's skyscrapers, had already begun when the forecast for heavy rain and strong winds on Thursday led to the delay.
The last time the parade was suspended was during World War Two, but it has never been postponed due to weather. In 1971, Macy's decided to ground the balloons, which often feature beloved characters from pop culture, because of weather.
A powerful coastal storm is set to affect the New York area in coming days.
The balloons will be deflated again and then re-inflated for Saturday
On Wednesday night, New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a state of emergency for Long Island, New York City and Westchester County
The potent nor'easter is expected to make it too windy and dangerous for the iconic balloons to fly.
Macy's had expected to put 100 inflatables into the sky to mark its 100th parade and feature 10 new balloons, including one depicting the animated dog Bluey wearing a crown and another showing a Minion character riding a banana like a horse.
"While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants and spectators is, and always will be, our top priority," said Will Cross, the parade's executive producer, during a news conference on Wednesday with city officials.
Cross also said the giant balloons would be deflated on Wednesday night and stored at a facility in neighbouring New Jersey until they were reinflated for the parade on Saturday.
Macy's confirmed the new parade date and updated a countdown clock on its website to reflect the Saturday schedule. Meanwhile, broadcaster NBC has said it will show the 2025 parade on Thursday.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who will not attend the parade on Saturday because of a scheduled surgery, said at the news conference that "you have to plan for every possibility" and confirmed that "extreme weather has forced" officials to make the change.
"We know that this is an inconvenience for many who come to visit our city. This decision, however, was made with safety being paramount," he said. "We want to ensure that we're delivering a parade that's not only incredible and spectacular, but one also that doesn't come at the expense of anyone's safety."
Mamdani also said that there would be an expanded police presence along the parade route on Saturday and that there were "no known specific or credible threats to the parade at this time".
Cross added that Macy's is working through what costs it could cover as a result of the delay and said the company is in contact with bands, performers and others who travelled to the city for the parade.
BBC Weather's Elizabeth Rizzini looks at the weather that will impact travel over US Thanksgiving.
During some past parades, strong winds and inclement weather have led to the tearing and deflation of the balloons as well as collisions with lampposts that caused injuries.
The US National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning, valid from 10:00 local time (15:00 GMT) on Thursday until 01:00 (06:00 GMT) on Friday with gusts potentially reaching 60mph (97km/h) - although the very strongest winds are likely to occur after the parade was due to end.
Heavy rain and coastal flooding will pose additional hazards across the eastern US as the storm sweeps through, while some inland parts could also see snow, BBC Weather reports.
The governor of the neighbouring state of New Jersey on Wednesday declared a state of emergency across the state's 21 counties, beginning at 18:00 local time (23:00 GMT).
Governor Mikie Sherrill's office said the powerful coastal storm is expected to bring damaging winds, heavy rainfall, and severe tidal flooding through Friday, with coastal and bayside communities facing the greatest risk. Sherrill urged residents to stay off the roads as much as possible once the storm arrives.
Originally called the Macy's Christmas Parade, the celebration, which also features live performers, debuted in 1924 as a way to boost holiday sales. It was founded by Macy's employees and their families.
From 1942 to 1944 New York went without the parade as the US directed materials like rubber and helium toward the country's war effort.
The 2.5mi (4km) procession route begins at Macy's Herald Square flagship store and concludes in Manhattan's Upper West Side, with performers and spectators lining the streets to greet Santa Claus and ring in the holiday season.
Country artist Megan Moroney and Grammy nominee Teddy Swims were slated to perform at the flagship store, but it is unclear whether they, along with the dozens of celebrities and float performers on the roster, would be returning on Saturday.

Storms targeting both US coasts threaten to snarl Thanksgiving travel for millions

OpenAI, ChatGPT'nin sohbet özelliği Chat ile daha kapsamlı görevlerin gerçekleştirildiği Work'ü tek bir deneyimde birleştirmeye başladı. Ancak şirketin bu değişikliği, özellikle ChatGPT'yi yoğun kullanan aboneler açısından yeni sınırlamalar getirebilir. OpenAI, kullanıcıların büyük bölümünün değişiklikten etkilenmeyeceğini belirtirken kullanımı en yoğun seviyede olan abonelerin mevcut kullanım limitlerine daha erken ulaşabileceğini ifade etti.
OpenAI'ın ürün yöneticilerinden Thibault Sottiaux, 24 Kasım'da X üzerinden yaptığı paylaşımda , birleştirilmiş Chat ve Work deneyiminin sınırlı sayıdaki Pro abonesine sunulmaya başlandığını açıkladı. Sottiaux, bu deneyimin daha geniş çaplı bir şekilde kullanıma sunulmadan önce kullanıcılardan geri bildirim toplamayı hedeflediklerini belirtti.
Paylaşılan bilgilere göre yeni düzenlemeyle birlikte Chat ve Work için ayrı ayrı olarak uygulanan kullanım limitleri birleştirilecek. Böylece ChatGPT'nin gelişmiş modelleri ve Codex üzerinden gerçekleştirilen işlemler aynı kullanım hakkından düşülecek.
OpenAI'ın destek sayfasında paylaştığı bilgilere göre değişiklik, aralık ayından itibaren Plus, Pro ve Business abonelerini kapsayacak. Kullanım miktarı, yapay zeka modellerinin işlediği ve ürettiği metni ölçmek için kullanılan token üzerinden hesaplanacak. Daha gelişmiş modeller ve karmaşık görevler, kullanıcıların mevcut haklarından daha fazla tüketebilecek. Bununla birlikte Instant modeliyle gerçekleştirilen sohbetler ortak kullanım hakkından düşülmeyecek . Kullanıcılar, gelişmiş modellere yönelik limitlerini doldurduktan sonra da Instant üzerinden sohbet etmeye devam edebilecek.
OpenAI sözcüsü, yaptığı açıklamada kullanıcıların büyük bölümünün kullanım haklarının yenilenmesini eskisinden daha sık beklemek zorunda kalmayacağını söyledi. Ancak ChatGPT'yi en yoğun kullanan küçük bir kullanıcı grubunun limitlerine daha erken ulaşabileceğini kabul etti.
Şirket, kullanıcıların kalan haklarını ve bu hakların ne zaman yenileneceğini Ayarlar bölümündeki Kullanım ekranından takip edebileceğini belirtiyor. Limitlerine ulaşan kullanıcılar, haklarının yenilenmesini bekleyebilecek, aboneliklerini yükseltebilecek veya uygun özellikleri kullanmaya devam etmek için ek kredi satın alabilecek.
OpenAI'ın kararı, özellikle gelişmiş akıl yürütme modellerini ve Codex'i yoğun kullanan aboneler arasında tartışma yarattı . Bazı kullanıcılar , daha önce ayrı ayrı yararlanabildikleri kullanım haklarının birleştirilmesiyle aynı abonelik ücretini ödemelerine rağmen gelişmiş modellere daha az erişebileceklerini düşünüyor . OpenAI ise sistemin daha verimli çalışması için iyileştirmelere devam edeceğini ve abonelerin mevcut paketlerinden daha fazla yararlanmasını hedeflediğini belirtiyor.

Türkiye’de de kullanılan şifre yönetim hizmeti sağlayıcısı 1Password bazı müşterilerine ait sınırlı miktarda hesap bilgisinin ele geçirildiğini fakat kullanıcı parolalarının güvende olduğunu bildirdi.
1Password tüm şifre, kredi kartı bilgileri ve hassas notlarınızı tek bir ana şifreyle (Master Password) saklama imkanı veren ücretli popüler bir şifre yönetim uygulaması.
Kanada merkezli uygulama 19 Kasım’da bir çalışanın kurumsal GitHub hesabına yetkisiz erişildiği bulgusu üzerine soruşturma başlattı. İnceleme sonundaysa bazı müşterilerine ait sınırlı miktarda hesap bilgisinin ele geçirildiğini fakat ‘parolalarının güvende olduğunu’ bildirdi.
– Saldırganın ele geçirdiği hesabı kullanarak kaynak kodlarına eriştiği ve arka uç hizmetlerine kötü amaçlı kod yüklediği tespit edildi. Bu kodla müşterilere ait yönetim verileri indirilmiş
– Saldırganın indirdiği hesap kayıtları müşteri isimleri ve e-posta adreslerinin yanısıra hesapla ilgili gizli olmayan dahili üst verileri içeriyor. Siber saldırgan kullanıcıların şifre kasalarına, bu kasalarda saklanan bilgilere ve kasaları koruyan anahtarlara erişmemiştir.
– Etkilenen GitHub hesabı devre dışı bırakıldı ve saldırganın erişimi engellendi. İfşa olmuş olabilecek tüm dahili kimlik bilgileri yenilenmiş veya iptal edilmişti. Kurtarma e-postalarında kullanılan kodların altı rakamdan on karaktere uzatılması gibi önlemler de alınmıştır.
– Müşterilerin çeşitli şekillerdeki kimlik avı girişimlerine karşı dikkatli olmalı. 1Password, sistemlerimizin ihlal edilmesi durumunda bile kasa içeriklerinizin açığa çıkmayacağı şekilde tasarlanmıştır. Kasanızdaki gizli bilgiler yalnızca sizin sahip olduğunuz anahtarlarla şifrelenir, bu nedenle ne biz ne de sunucularımıza giren bir saldırgan bunlara erişebilir.
Son dönemde ABD ve Avrupa çeşitli alanlarda siber saldırılara maruz kalıyor.
ABD Başkanı Donald Trump hava ulaşımı, bankacılık ve ulusal güvenlik sistemlerini etkileyen siber saldırıların ardınan Beyaz Saray Ulusal Siber Güvenlik Direktörü Sean Cairncross’u görevden aldı.
ABD Federal Soruşturma Bürosu (FBI), bilgisayar korsanlarının dünya genelinde siber saldırıları otonomlaştırmak amacıyla yapay zeka destekli bir araç kullandığını duyurdu .
AB’deyse süpermarketlerin soğutma sistemlerine düzenlenen siber saldırıların on milyonlarca avroya mal olduğu tahmin ediliyor.
Birlik, siber güvenlik için 16 Ocak 2023’te NIS2 Direktifi’ni (Ağ ve Bilgi Güvenliği Direktifi 2) yürürlüğe sokmuştu. Avrupa Komisyonu 27 üye ülkeye yasalarını direktifle uyumlu hale getirmesi için 17 Ekim 2024’e kadar süre vermiş, ‘gereğini yapmayan’ 23 ülkeye ihtar göndermişti.
Komisyon daha sonra 19 ülkenin süreci başarıyla tamamladığını belirterek uyum sürecini tamamlamadığını tespit ettiği İspanya, Fransa, İrlanda ve Hollanda’yı AB Adalet Divanı’na sevk etmişti.
Komisyonun Teknolojik Egemenlik, Güvenlik ve Demokrasiden Sorumlu Başkan Yardımcısı Henna Virkkunen, 11 Kasım’da “Son günlerdeki bazı siber saldırılar AB kuralları etkin şekilde uygulansaydı önlenebilirdi” dedi.

Beaches close as Los Angeles and La Jolla see all-time high tides and big waves batter landmark pier in Pacifica
Super El Niño weather brought record-breaking high tides up and down the California coast on Wednesday, sending seawater rushing into beachside communities and flooding roads and businesses.
As big waves battered the coast, the tip of a landmark pier in Pacifica, south of San Francisco, was slammed into the sea, local news outlets reported . The pier, which had once housed a favorite local cafe , had previously suffered structural damage and had been closed to the public, the San Francisco Chronicle reported , and collapsed after contact with ocean swells 12 times stronger than on an average November day.
Los Angeles and Santa Barbara tied or broke all-time high tide records on Wednesday, at 8.19 and 8.21ft, respectively, according to the National Weather Service (NWS). La Jolla, California, just north of San Diego, also set an all-time high tide record of 8.11ft (2.5 meters), according to the NWS, while preliminary data suggested that tides in Monterey, south of San Francisco, might also have set an all-time record at 8.03ft .
The city of Monterey closed multiple beaches to the public over safety concerns, with closures lasting until Friday. Beaches in Santa Cruz county were also closed.
“That sun may be out, but the beach and surf zone remain dangerous,” NWS San Francisco warned, citing waves around the San Francisco Bay area as high as 24ft.
“This is a preview of things to come,” California’s governor, Gavin Newsom, said in a San Francisco press conference about Wednesday’s flooding. “That’s why it’s so important that we not just situationally address and reflect on moments like this, but sustainably get under the hood and try to solve for some of these things.”
In Pacifica, giant waves and tide waters swept over beaches and piers, flooding coastal roads including Highway 1 near the famous local landmark Taco Bell Cantina, America’s poshest Taco Bell. (The iconic restaurant was unharmed by the tides, NBC Bay Area reported .)
“This El Niño is unprecedented with its strength,” the San Mateo county supervisor Ray Mueller told the Los Angeles Times . “For this to be happening when it is a beautiful day on the coast side today, in clear sunshine and no wind, is really significant.”
Multiple coastal homes in Sunset Beach, in Orange county, had flooded, the Los Angeles Times reported , but a local fire chief said the overall damage had been mitigated by how aggressively local homeowners had fortified their homes in advance.
Low-lying coastal roads around the Bay Area also saw flooding, including a stretch of road near the Golden Gate Bridge, which was temporarily closed, the Chronicle reported.
However, most of the state avoided the worst-case scenario – coastal flooding amplified by intense winter rainstorms.
“We’re past high tide, and San Francisco has made it through the worst of this round of king tides,” mayor Daniel Lurie said in a social media statement just after noon local time, saying officials were “only aware of minimal impacts across the city”.
Local officials had been preparing for weeks for the risk that flooding would disrupt travel during Thanksgiving week, one of the busiest times of the year. Experts warn that flooding risk will only worsen in the next two months.
Flooding risk at the San Francisco international airport, a major transit hub situated on low-lying coastal land, had been of particular concern. At least three airlines offered free trip changes to travelers whose journeys took them through San Francisco on Wednesday, the San Francisco Chronicle reported .
But the airport announced at noon that “We’re in the clear,” and said it was deactivating its emergency operations center after avoiding any impact from the high tides on Tuesday and Wednesday.
On the north coast, the NWS reported that Humboldt Bay saw its second highest tide on record, and advised residents to prepare for major coastal flooding in low lying areas. The county sheriff warned the public to stay away from beaches during the storm.
A local news outlet in Oregon shared a video on Tuesday that illustrated the risk of the west coast’s high-tide surf, showing a man and his dog almost getting swept away by unexpectedly high waves during the king tides in Cannon Beach, Oregon. Both man and dog escaped without injury, police told KVAL News .
The California governor’s office of emergency services deployed crews and equipment around the state to assist with storm response. In the Bay Area, crews could be seen preparing sandbags to help protect buildings from flooding.
California’s flooding risk this week is the result of a combination of factors, some of them driven by this year’s super El Niño weather, including the lingering effects of the massive Kelvin wave that traveled up California’s coast. The overlap of unusually high Pacific coast water levels this year with the seasonal high tides called “king tides” has sparked alarm from weather experts, who have warned that the most dangerous flooding is likely to occur if a strong winter storm with heavy wind and rain hits areas of the coast at the same time as the high tide’s peak.
So far, it seems like California has avoided the worst of that risk during the November king tide period. But the amplified king tides will return twice more, around late December and then in late January, in periods where big winter storms remain likely.

A powerful storm forecast to bring fierce winds and heavy rain to the northeastern United States has forced the unprecedented postponement of the city's 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade, with the event rescheduled for Saturday. Officials warned that Thursday's conditions could bring down tree limbs and power lines, while posing a safety risk to the parade's giant balloons and the crowds below.
Department store Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade will also be a first, as organisers made an unprecedented decision to postpone the event to Saturday because of bad weather .
The annual parade – originally scheduled for Thursday – has been moved “out of an abundance of caution" and following consultation with city officials about the severe weather, Macy's said in a statement Wednesday.
“Our team is now working through the complex operational logistics required to bring the Parade to life on Saturday, and we will share additional details as they are finalised,” the company said.
The postponement came as New York City is set to get slammed by a storm bringing intense winds and rain to the region, which had raised worries about how the parade's massive balloons would fare while floating through the windswept canyons between Manhattan’s skyscrapers and over throngs of spectators lining the streets below.
At a news conference, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday's winds will be strong enough to snap tree limbs and down power lines, and he stressed that rescheduling the parade was the right call.
“Now, I know that many New Yorkers, myself included, as well as millions around the world, were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow," he said. “Generation after generation has watched SpongeBob and Spider-Man soar down our streets and has taken in Garfield floating down 6th Avenue. And I know that this change of plans will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first.”
The National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning and a coastal flood warning for Thursday into Friday. The city's emergency management agency has been warning residents about the possible storm, with officials banning empty tractor-trailers from bridges Thursday morning because of the wind.

NBC, which airs the parade, said it will instead broadcast a rerun of the 2025 edition Thursday. It was not immediately clear whether the event’s expansive lineup would also shift to the new date, though representatives for Broadway shows “Chicago” and “Hamilton” said their performers will make the switch to Saturday.
The parade's iconic balloons were well on the way to being inflated when the postponement was announced. Macy’s representatives had repeatedly put off interviews on-site, raising eyebrows among the city's news media ahead of the official postponement.
Will Coss, a Macy's executive, said organisers are working with bands and other performers and are “optimistic that we're going to be able to maintain the parade that we set out to produce and to deliver to New York City on Thanksgiving.”

High king tides threaten California coastline, flood communities
Coastal areas of California are bracing for potential flooding as king tides peak in the state during the US Thanksgiving holiday.
Water levels across the US state's vast coastline could reach over 8ft (2.4 metres) in some areas on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the National Weather Service (NWS) - breaking records set just last month.
The NWS has warned parts of California could face major coastal flooding, which is likely to be significant in low-lying areas. There have already been some reports of flooding.
Meanwhile, storms are also forecast for the Pacific Northwest, including the Canadian province of British Columbia, and eastern parts of the US.
Portions of a pier in northern California came crashing down into the ocean on Wednesday as high tides and strong waves battered the structure, video showed.
Beachgoers have been advised to stay away from the water's edge as large waves could suddenly form. Such waves could be damaging to piers and jetties, and could capsize small vessels, the NWS warned.
Flooding has already been reported in the San Francisco Bay Area.
In San Diego, a high tide of 8 ft 11in was recorded on Wednesday morning local time - potentially breaking the record for highest tide measured in the area, which was just set late last month at 7.98ft.
In Los Angeles, the tide on Wednesday was thought to be as high 8.19 - the record for the city that was set only weeks ago 27 October when parts of the California coast experienced flooding.
Recently set high tide records were also broken in Santa Barbara and La Jolla, according to preliminary data.
King tides are the highest predicted tide of the year and are above the highest water level reached at high tide on an average day.
While they typically occur once or twice a year in most coastal areas, they are happening more frequently in some as sea levels rise. These king tides are being strengthened by the strongest El Niño weather pattern on record.
Storm systems are also expected to impact the US through the Thanksgiving holiday - one affecting the Pacific Northwest and another the eastern part of the country, the US National Weather Service said.
On the east coast, a developing Nor'easter storm is expected to bring heavy rain, strong winds, and coastal flooding.
Major impacts are expected to begin on Wednesday across the southeast, and move northward Wednesday night and on Thursday, the NWS said.
"Those along the eastern seaboard can expect gusty, possibly damaging winds, heavy rain, and major coastal and marine impacts," it added.
The developing storm system could bring about one to four inches rain along America's east coast and a peak of four to six inches in coastal North Carolina.
The US department store chain Macy's has postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York, which was due to take place on Thursday, until Saturday because of severe weather - the first time this has happened.
The stormy weather on both coasts could disrupt travel for millions of people.
The American Automobile Association (AAA) has predicted that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles (80km) from home for Thanksgiving between Tuesday 24 November and Monday 30 November.
Officials have also issued a flood warning along Vancouver's coastline in Canada's most western province of British Columbia.
Residents were urged to take "immediate action to protect life and property", a weather warning from Environment and Climate Change Canada said.
King tides were expected to potentially increase already high water levels there too.

Andy Taylor, who has died aged 65, was the wild boy of Duran Duran.
In the early 1980s, the pop legends sold over 100 million records and dominated the charts in both Britain and the United States.
But success came at a cost. For Taylor, global superstardom became a cocaine and alcohol fuelled nightmare that left him burnt out and battling clinical depression.
"For sure, we paraded around in our fast cars with beautiful models on yachts in the south of France without needing to pay the bill," he later wrote.
Andrew Taylor was born in North Tyneside on 16 February 1961.
Home was Cullercoats, a coastal village near Whitley Bay where many people, including his uncles, depended on the sea for their livelihoods.
At first, it was a happy childhood. There was church on Sunday with his parents, Ronnie and Blanche, followed by games of football on the beach with younger brother Ronnie junior.
On Christmas Day, his extended family would belt out Bing Crosby hits around the piano.
Andy Taylor's childhood was blighted when his mother abandoned the family without explanation
The 11-year-old returned home to find his father in the kitchen, silently weeping. Taylor's mother, it seemed, had simply disappeared. There wasn't even a note.
"It was like a guillotine had suddenly come rushing down," he recalled. It "sliced everything apart without explanation as to why I was guilty".
After that, occasional meetings with his mother were chilly encounters with no explanation offered. Taylor never discovered why she had left.
Having worked hard to pass his 11-plus exams, Taylor rapidly went off the rails.
He skipped school and spent many days in remote caves on the beach, drinking cider and smoking dried banana skins. He'd heard absurd rumours this would get him high.
Salvation lay in a guitar he found hidden in his father's cupboard and a BBC Two programme that taught him the basic chords.
Andy Taylor's earliest performances were in working men's clubs in the north-east of England
By the age of 16, he was working on a building site and playing in a band.
Taylor and his friends performed at working men's clubs across the north-east of England, often providing musical accompaniment for strippers.
A contract to provide entertainment for American troops in Germany included a clause stipulating that he did six hours a night on stage.
On his return, Taylor saw an advert seeking a "livewire guitarist" for a new band based in the West Midlands.
He called the number and "made that fateful train journey to Birmingham".
Duran Duran, named after a character in Jane Fonda's space-sex movie Barbarella, were to be based in a club called the Rum Runner.
On arrival, he met bassist John Taylor and drummer Roger Taylor - all unrelated.
Keyboardist Nick Rhodes followed and, after a short search, Simon Le Bon, the lead singer, appeared "looking like an Elvis who'd been to the chip shop".
Andy Taylor's initial impression of Simon Le Bon was that he looked like Elvis who'd been to a chip shop
They didn't waste time. Within six weeks, the group had pulled together enough material for an album.
Andy Taylor's musical challenge was to work out how his guitar fitted a post-punk age of electronic music, while Le Bon's lyrics and melody skated over the top.
A record deal with EMI gave the group the production support they needed.
Planet Earth was released on 21 February 1981. It raced towards the top 10, winning them a coveted slot on Top of the Pops.
Six months later, Girls on Film reached number five in the UK charts.
The New Romantic revolution, as much about fashion as music, was under way.
The boys discovered that their Antony Price suits and make-up gave them something to talk about with girls in the clubs.
And there were soon girls everywhere, thanks to a marketing campaign that pushed the band heavily in teen magazines.
After one US concert, the band swept the stage and supposedly counted 2,000 teddy bears, 150 pairs of knickers, 300 bras and dozens of hotel room keys that had been thrown from the crowd.
Andy Taylor said life with Duran Duran was like entering Narnia in The Lion, The Witch and The Wardrobe
"We were just working-class escapists who wanted to live out our dreams," explained Taylor. "We didn't want to be like UB40 and The Specials singing about unemployment and urban decay."
Duran Duran embarked on exhausting foreign tours to drive sales, and their flamboyant videos, made at huge cost, played constantly on MTV in the US.
A bandmate pushed Taylor off a yacht while shooting the video for Rio, and he nearly drowned off the Caribbean coast amid a swarm of poisonous jellyfish.
In Sri Lanka, the group was forced to flee when 4,000 furious monks objected to their using a holy site as a backdrop to Hungry Like the Wolf.
Then, having smoked dope and drunk a bottle of Jack Daniel's, Taylor climbed a tree with his guitar for a spectacular shot.
He fell into a muddy lagoon that was used by local elephants as a latrine and spent four days in hospital recovering from a tropical infection.
By now, Taylor's original £50-a-week retainer from EMI was a distant memory.
He shared a flat in Moseley with Le Bon, took prodigious quantities of cocaine, and worked his way through the flocks of page three girls who frequented the Rum Runner.
Andy Taylor married Tracey Wilson on Hollywood's Sunset Strip in 1982
Then he met Tracey Wilson, a level-headed hair salon manager.
Initially, she had doubts about becoming romantically involved with a self-confessed womanising, drug-taking guitarist.
She was eventually persuaded and, on his 21st birthday, Taylor proposed. The couple remained together for more than 40 years and had four children.
Famously, Duran Duran were Princess Diana's favourite band. This too, came with risks.
In June 1983, the IRA tried to assassinate the Prince and Princess of Wales while they watched the group perform live at Tottenham Court Road's Dominion Theatre.
The plot, which involved planting a bomb in the toilets, was stopped by British intelligence.
Fortunately, the IRA man sent to plant the device turned out to be a double agent, who tipped off MI5 and fled to Paris.
Princess Diana met Duran Duran 1983. Unbeknownst to Andy Taylor (far right) the IRA were plotting to bomb the venue
The same year, Is There Something I Should Know? became Duran Duran's fastest-selling song to date.
The Reflex, which their record company initially refused to release, also topped the charts on both sides of the Atlantic.
The American press called them the Fab Five, in comparison to the Beatles, and their vast earnings caused them to become tax exiles.
For Andy Taylor, foreign tours had become increasingly drug-fuelled with so-called "rock docs" injecting him with chemicals to get through sets.
The constant use of cocaine made him nervy and irrational. The BBC threatened to ban him from their Saturday Superstore programme when he swore at a caller.
Headlines about Taylor's drug use at the Rum Runner damaged the band's hitherto squeaky-clean image.
In Birmingham, the club was suddenly served with a compulsory purchase order by the council and bulldozed.
Their Wild Boys video featured Simon Le Bon strapped to a huge waterwheel. But it was Andy Taylor who felt as if he was drowning.
Andy Taylor (sitting in a cardboard box) and Simon Le Bon behind the scenes at Live Aid in 1985
As a guitarist, he wanted to make records with a harder rock edge, which led to The Power Station - a band he put together with Robert Palmer while killing time between Duran Duran tours.
But it was his lifestyle that was worrying him. After years of living on Big Macs and cocaine, he knew he was heading for a breakdown.
After Live Aid in 1985, the constant bickering between members of the band led to a prolonged separation.
When they ran out of money, Duran Duran's original line-up reformed to work on new projects.
They continued to sell plenty of tickets for live shows to die-hard fans, but new records had disappointing sales.

Pitt filed the lawsuit against Jolie in 2022 after she sold her stake in Château Miraval, saying she broke their agreement not to sell their interests
Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have settled a years-long legal battle over their French winery, according to a joint statement from the former Hollywood couple.
“We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” representatives for Jolie and Pitt said in a statement. “Any comments in media stories attributed to ‘sources’ are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us.”
Both sides have moved to dismiss claims against each other. The terms of the agreement were not made public.
The couple had bought a controlling interest in Château Miraval in 2008, and married there in 2014.
Jolie initiated divorce proceedings in 2016, and the couple was declared legally single in 2019, although their divorce settlement continued to play out until 2024 . Jolie was cleared to sell her share in 2021 for $164m (£125.06m) before their wider financial settlement was finalized.
Pitt filed the lawsuit against Jolie in February 2022, after the actor sold her stake in the French winery to the Stoli Group, a spirits maker controlled by oligarch Yuri Shefler. In the suit, Pitt said Jolie had broken their agreement not to sell their interests in the winery without the other’s consent after she sold her stake to the Russian businessman.
In October 2022, Jolie filed a counter lawsuit against Pitt, which for the first time described alleged abusive behavior that led to their divorce. The actor’s attorneys said negotiations for Jolie to sell her share in the winery to Pitt broke down over his demand that she sign “a nondisclosure agreement that would have contractually prohibited her from speaking outside of court about Pitt’s physical and emotional abuse of her and their children”. Pitt denied the accusations.

Watch: Andy Taylor tells the BBC about his cancer diagnosis in 2023
Andy Taylor, the guitarist for the pop group Duran Duran, has died at the age of 65.
Born in Tynemouth, he co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits, including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film; and also worked with artists like Robert Palmer, Rod Stewart and Belinda Carlisle.
In a statement, his bandmates said Taylor had fought "a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer" and "passed away peacefully at home, surrounded by his family, on Monday 23 November".
His wife, Tracey, said the musician "was the rock of our family", adding: "We will miss him every single day".
Andy Taylor: Duran Duran's livewire guitarist who was a Wild Boy on stage and off
The son of a fisherman, Taylor taught himself guitar, bass, and drums and began playing professionally at age 13.
He played with several bands around the UK before answering a music paper advertisement for a "live-wire guitarist", which led to his audition for Duran Duran in Birmingham in April 1980.
The group went on to achieve global fame through the New Romantic movement, which combined slick, melodic synth-pop with aspirational music videos and chiselled good looks.
Andy Taylor's guitar riffs powered some of Duran Duran's best-known songs
Taylor's guitar lines - full of glassy, powerful riffs - were often a highlight of their songs, from the choppy opening of Girls on Film to the sleazy scuzz of Hungry Like The Wolf.
"Andy was there at the very beginning of our story," said his bandmates Simon Le Bon, Nick Rhodes, John Taylor and Roger Taylor (his bandmates were unrelated, despite sharing the same last name).
"From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music.
"His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.
"Our thoughts are with his wife Tracey, his children Georgina, Isabella, Bethany and Andrew, and grandson Albie. They all loved him deeply and we ask that their privacy be respected at this very difficult time."
Sir Rod Stewart, who wrote five songs with Taylor for the 1988 album Out of Order, paid tribute to his "dear pal".
"We made some good music together and at the same time had some outrageous fun," Sir Rod posted on Instagram.
Taylor quit Duran Duran at the height of their fame in 1985, but rejoined the band several times in the 2000s and contributed to their most recent album, Danse Macabre
Duran Duran were one of the biggest pop acts of the 1980s, and its five members became global hearththrobs.
Their indelible hooks and airbrushed music videos found a natural home on the newly launched MTV, giving their career a huge boost in the US.
They became so popular in the States that the press labeled them the leaders of a "Second British Invasion" of the charts - alongside groups like Spandau Ballet, Human League and Eurythmics.
During a hiatus in 1984, Andy and John Taylor enlisted Robert Palmer for their successful but short-lived side project the Power Station.
Duran Duran bridged the sounds of pop, funk, disco, punk and new wave with a sound that remains indelibly tied to the 1980s
The following year, the guitarist decided to quit Duran Duran, after a miserable experience performing at Live Aid.
"We'd reached rock bottom and we had absolutely nothing to say to each other," he wrote in his autobiography, Wild Boy.
"We drove to the venue through streets packed with excited rock fans, but inside the bus the atmosphere was as if we were on a way to a funeral."
He went on to play on Robert Palmer's Addicted To Love, and released a solo album, Thunder, in 1987.
After a period writing and producing albums for other artists, he rejoined Duran Duran in 2000, lasting for just one album (2004's Astronaut) before parting ways again.
In 2022, when the band were inducted to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Taylor was notably absent from the ceremony, despite public plans for a reunion.
When the group took the stage, singer Simon Le Bon read a letter from the guitarist, in which he revealed his diagnosis with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer.
Nonetheless, he contributed to the following year's Halloween-themed album Danse Macabre, marking his final collaboration with the band.
Taylor (second left) married his wife Tracey at the Chateau Marmont hotel in Los Angeles in 1982
"Andy never took the easy musical route," said Le Bon in a personal statement marking his friend's death.
"His overdrive, overdrove us into being the only funk/rock/punk band in the New Romantic movement, with songs that still survive, decades later.
"There's a massive Andy Taylor shaped hole in my heart. It'll never close up; I won't let it. I will miss him & love him for all my days."
Taylor is survived by his wife, Tracey, a hairstylist he met during the early days of Duran Duran, and whom he married in 1982.
"For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first," she wrote in her statement.
"Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home."
She continued: "Andy faced the last few years with so much courage and determination. He never gave up, fighting until the very end, never losing his love of life.
"The kindness and support shown to him by fans from all over the world throughout his illness brought him immense comfort and strength, and for that we will always be grateful."

Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have settled a long-running legal battle over her sale of a stake in their French vineyard, which unfolded amid a bitter divorce.
"We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further," said the Hollywood stars' representatives in a joint statement.
They bought a controlling interest in Château Miraval in 2008 and wed there six years later.
In the lawsuit, Pitt , 62 , argued that Jolie, 51, acted without his permission in selling her share in the winery to a Russian oligarch. She counter-sued, accusing Pitt of drunkenly attacking her and their children on a flight, prompting her to file for divorce in 2016.
The settlement announced on Wednesday resolves both of their respective legal actions.
"Any comments in media stories attributed to 'sources' are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us," said the statement from their representatives.
Pitt's lawsuit had accused Jolie of seeking "to inflict harm" on him when she sold her stake in their co-owned vineyard, which he claimed had forced him to partner with "a stranger with poisonous associations and intentions".
The Fight Club star said he and Jolie had agreed not to sell their stakes in the venue without the permission of the other.
It was alleged that Jolie had sold her share to a Luxembourg-based spirits manufacturer controlled by Russian oligarch Yuri Shefler, without Pitt's knowledge.
Jolie hit back with her own lawsuit, accusing Pitt of grabbing her by the head and attacking two of their children during a 2016 private jet flight trip.
Pitt also verbally abused and poured alcohol on his family during the flight from France to Los Angeles, her lawsuit had alleged.
Her lawyers alleged Pitt began shouting, accusing her of being "too deferential" to their six children - aged eight to 15 at the time.
Pitt was not charged following a police investigation into the incident and he denied the allegations.
They reached a divorce settlement late last year after an eight-year legal battle.
It is understood that Pitt's litigation with Stoli Group, a beverage company owned by the Russian oligarch, is ongoing.
At the time of their 2014 marriage, Pitt and Jolie were among the most lucrative names in Hollywood.
They met on the set of the 2005 film Mr and Mrs Smith and were soon dubbed Brangelina by the press.
The marriage was Pitt's second after a relationship with Friends star Jennifer Aniston.
It was Jolie's third, after actors Billy Bob Thornton and Jonny Lee Miller.
Jolie adopted her first child, Maddox, from Cambodia in 2002 a few months after he was born. Pitt later adopted him after he and Jolie had begun their relationship.
In 2005, the pair adopted daughter Zahara from Ethiopia when she was a few months old.
The couple's first biological child, Shiloh, was born in Namibia in 2006.
Their son Pax was adopted at the age of three from Vietnam in 2007, and twins Knox and Vivienne were born in 2008.
Since the couple split, four of the six children have legally changed their last name to Jolie rather than Jolie-Pitt, according to court filings citied by Hollywood press.

Rescuers in Indonesia on Thursday were contending with rising water, darkness and steep, slippery ground as they combed the site in Bogor regency, a mountainous area south of the capital Jakarta.
Rescuers say they are searching for 13 more miners believed trapped by flooding in an illegal gold mine where 13 bodies were recovered earlier.
The disaster began late on Monday, when heavy rain made the Ciseureuh River burst its banks and pour into a mine shaft, which is estimated to be around 100 metres deep. Miners were digging for gold at the time.
Some escaped from one section of the excavation before the shaft filled with water.
Authorities said the illegal nature of the operation meant they were not alerted straight away. Local miners and residents first tried to pump out the water themselves until the situation spiralled out of control.
Police received the first reports of trapped miners some 16 hours after the flooding. The nearby state-owned mining company PT Antam passed a formal report to the Jakarta Search and Rescue Agency shortly after midnight on Wednesday, which set a full-scale operation in motion.
Teams have been using submersible pumps to drain the shaft and working to seal openings where groundwater is seeping in.
On Thursday, 325 personnel concentrated on two adjacent shafts, using rope-access techniques to reach victims, said agency chief Desiana Kartika Bahari.
The flooded shaft lies close to facilities run by PT Antam's Pongkor gold mining unit. The company said the incident had nothing to do with its operations.
Informal mining is widespread in Indonesia, where thousands of people work in hazardous conditions.
Miners risk landslides, flooding and tunnel collapses, while gold processing often exposes them to toxic mercury and cyanide with little or no protective equipment.

At least 31 people were killed and 15 injured when a fuel truck overturned and burst into flames on a busy highway in Cairo on Wednesday, engulfing nearby vehicles, Egyptian authorities said.
A fire erupted in Egyptian capital Cairo on Wednesday killing at least 31 people, the health ministry said, after a fuel truck reportedly overturned on a packed highway.
AFP footage showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital's Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists sounded their horns and scrambled to get away. Surrounding buildings appeared to escape the flames.
State media reported that the fire broke out when a truck loaded with fuel overturned on Cairo's Ring Road – a crowded highway linking different parts of the capital – and burst into flames, engulfing nearby vehicles.
The health ministry said 39 ambulances were sent to the scene and 15 people were taken to hospital with injuries, four of them in critical condition.
"The scene was terrifying," Abdel Rahman Khalil told AFP, saying he arrived shortly after the crash and saw the overturned fuel truck engulfed in flames.
AFP images showed a grisly aftermath with cars burned out, as firefighters doused the truck's wreckage.
Egypt's public prosecutor said an investigation had been opened and DNA tests were being carried out to identify badly burned victims.
The health ministry said it had raised its emergency alert level and Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar had travelled to the scene and nearby hospitals.
The health minister's spokesman told state-linked al-Qahera News that "the Ring Road has been reopened, and the remnants of the accident have been cleared."
Footage carried by Al-Qahera News showed the charred truck's wreckage being removed, while traffic partially resumed around it.
A spokesperson for the Egyptian Cabinet told local media that Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly had ordered an investigation into the causes of the accident.
He said the government was awaiting a full clarification before determining "future measures regarding the transport of petroleum products and ensuring safety and security during such transport operations".
Egypt, with its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, has suffered several deadly fires in recent years.
Fire escapes, smoke detectors and alarms are rare and in many areas, warrens of narrow roads make it hard for fire engines to reach disaster sites.
Car crashes are also common, and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted.
Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt's state statistics agency.
The year before, more than 5,200 road deaths were recorded across the country, according to authorities.
