AK Parti, Yenilenebilir Enerji Kaynaklarının Elektrik Enerjisi Üretimi Amaçlı Kullanımına İlişkin Kanun ile Bazı Kanunlarda Değişiklik Yapılmasına Dair Kanun Teklifi'nin TBMM Başkanlığına sundu.
AK Parti Grup Başkanı Abdullah Güler, Meclis'e sunulan düzenlemeyle ilgili, "1 Ocak 2017 tarihinden öncesine ait ödenmemiş Genel Sağlık Sigortası prim borçları ile bunlara bağlı gecikme cezası ve zamlarının tamamının tahsilinden vazgeçiyoruz. Bu bağlamda 2 milyon 199 bin 869 vatandaşımızın toplamda 5 milyar 627 milyon 666 bin lira tutarındaki prim borcunu terkin ederek, üzerindeki borç yükünü kaldırıyor, sağlık hizmetlerine yine kesintisiz ve kolay erişimi teminat altına alıyoruz. Kamu üniversite sağlık hizmeti sunucularımızın 2026 yılı götürü bedel sözleşmelerinden kaynaklanan tahakkuk farklarını terkin ederek, hastanelerimizin finansal sürdürülebilirliğini ve sağlık hizmetinin devamını sağlamış oluyoruz." ifadelerini kullanmıştı.
TBMM Genel Kurulunda, Yenilenebilir Enerji Kaynaklarının Elektrik Enerjisi Üretimi Amaçlı Kullanımına İlişkin Kanun ile Bazı Kanunlarda Değişiklik Yapılmasına Dair Kanun Teklifi'nin görüşmelerine başlandı.
Teklifin tümü üzerinde söz alan Yeni Yol Partisi Grup Başkanvekili Selçuk Özdağ, kanun teklifinin içerisindeki düzenlemelerin 10 ayrı kanunda değişiklik öngördüğünü anlatarak, torba kanun yapımına ilişkin eleştirilerde bulundu.
Düzenlemeyle yenilenebilir enerji üretimi yapacaklara yeni mali engeller çıkarılacağını öne süren Özdağ, şunları söyledi:
"Türkiye'nin güneş ve rüzgardan daha fazla enerji üretmesine hiç kimse karşı çıkmaz. Her yıl enerji ithalatına milyarlarca dolar para ödüyorsunuz. Dış ticaret açığımızın önemli bir bölümü enerji ithalatından kaynaklanıyor. Hal böyleyken kendi imkanlarıyla elektrik üreten vatandaşın, sanayicinin, müteşebbisin önüne yeni mali engeller çıkarmak istemenin bir sebebi olmalı. Yenilenebilir enerjide atacağınız her adım, yapacağınız her yeni yatırım, cari açığın azalmasını sağlayacak. O halde bu yatırımlara mali engeller çıkarmanın amacı nedir?"
İYİ Parti Genel Başkan Yardımcısı ve İstanbul Milletvekili Buğra Kavuncu, "kanun teklifinin, Tasfiyesine Karar Verilen Bazı Yatırım Fonları Hakkında Kanun'a madde eklenmesi için hazırlandığını" belirterek, fon soruşturmasına ilişkin değerlendirme ve eleştirilerde bulundu.
Düzenleme kapsamında 1 Ocak 2017'den önceye ait ödenmemiş genel sağlık sigortası primleri ile gecikme cezası ve gecikme zammı gibi feri alacaklarının tamamının tahsilinden vazgeçileceğini aktaran Kavuncu, "Ülke öyle bir hale geldi ki sürekli af bekleyen, yüklerden kurtulmayı bekleyen yoğun nüfusumuz var. Bunun yanında vaktinde bütün vergilerini ödeyen ve sonra da 'Ben bunları ödüyorsam bu af niye çıkıyor?' diye soran haklı vatandaşlarımız var. Maalesef böyle bir düzen yarattı bu zihniyet." dedi.
CHP Bolu Milletvekili Türker Ateş, kanun teklifini eleştirerek, "günü kurtaracak düzenlemelerle geçici kanunlar yapıldığını" ileri sürdü.
Düzenleme kapsamında, kamu-üniversite hastaneleri 2026 yılındaki götürü bedel sözleşmesi farklarının terkin edileceğini anlatan Ateş, "Üniversite hastanelerimizin ayakta kalması için bu maddeye olumlu bakıyoruz ancak 2020'den bu yana tam 6 kez aynı geçici maddeyi getirdiniz. Demek ki üniversite hastanesi finansman modeli çökmüş vaziyette. Tıp eğitimi veren, araştırma yapan bu kurumlara kalıcı bir gelir ödeme sistemi kurulmalıdır." diye konuştu.
"YENİLENEBİLİR ENERJİ, YENİ İSTİHDAM ALANLARI OLUŞTURMA FIRSATIDIR"
MHP Antalya Milletvekili Abdurrahman Başkan, enerji politikalarına yalnızca bugünün ihtiyaçları üzerinden bakamayacaklarını, enerji arz güvenliğinin, ekonomik kalkınma, sanayinin rekabet gücü ve milli güvenliğin asla birbirinden ayrı düşünülemeyeceğini vurguladı.
"Enerjide dışa bağımlılığın azaltılması, yerli kaynaklarımızın etkin biçimde değerlendirilmesi ve altyapımızın güçlendirilmesi, Türkiye'nin geleceği bakımından temel hedeflerimiz arasında yer almalıdır." ifadesini kullanan Başkan, enerji arz güvenliği açısından doğal gaz altyapısının esnek ve ihtiyaçlara cevap verebilmesinin büyük önem taşıdığını kaydetti.
Yenilenebilir enerji kaynaklarının önemini vurgulayan Başkan, şunları kaydetti:
"Yenilenebilir enerji, aynı zamanda teknoloji geliştirme, yerli sanayiyi büyütme ve yeni istihdam alanları oluşturma fırsatıdır. Bu kaynakların doğru planlanması, teknolojik gelişmelerle desteklenmesi ve enerji sistemimize güvenilir biçimde entegre edilmesi Türkiye'nin uzun vadeli kalkınma hedefleri açısından büyük önem taşımaktadır."
DEM Parti İzmir Milletvekili İbrahim Akın, kanun teklifinin "torba kanun" şeklinde görüşülmesinin TBMM'ye yakışmadığını belirterek, eleştirilerde bulundu.
Teklifteki bazı maddelerin iktidarın enerji politikalarıyla ilgili sürdürdüğü durumu açığa çıkardığını dile getiren Akın, "Özellikle tarlaları, meraları, kuralsız bir şekilde 'yenilenebilir enerji' diye bahsedilen enerji politikasıyla devam ettirmeye çalışıyorsunuz. Oysa dünyada artık bu enerji politikaları tartışılıyor." şeklinde konuştu.
Hükümetin "yenilenebilir enerji" kapsamında "güneş tarlaları" yaptığını anlatan Akın, bunun mevcut iklim krizini daha çok artırdığını iddia etti.
Yeni Parti Kocaeli Milletvekili Nail Çiler, 15 maddelik kanun teklifinin çok karışık olduğunu savunarak, "İstihdam ve teşviklerden BOTAŞ'ın vergi borçlarına, üniversite hastanelerinden genel sağlık sigortasına, kurumlar vergisinden yatırım fonlarının tasfiyesine kadar birbirinden tamamen farklı konular önümüze gelmiş durumda. Bir polis adayının eğitim hakkı ile bir enerji yatırımcısının lisans bedeli, bir üniversite hastanesinin finansman sorunu, yatırım fonu mağdurlarının tazminat hakkı neden aynı torbaya kondu?" sorusunu yöneltti.
Teklif kapsamında Mesleki Eğitim Kanunu'nda yapılacak değişiklikle, aday çırak, çırak, işletmelerde mesleki eğitim gören, staj veya tamamlayıcı eğitime devam eden öğrencilere verilen ücretlere sağlanan devlet katkısında Cumhurbaşkanına tanınan uzatma yetkisinin süresine ilişkin düzenleme yapıldığını aktaran Çiler, "Mesleki eğitime ilişkin devlet katkısını uzatmak kadar çocuklarımızın iş güvenliğini sağlamak zorundayız." dedi.
Konutlarda doğal gaz ve elektrikteki KDV oranının yüzde 1'e indirilmesi gerektiğini savunan Çiler, ayrıca bireysel şekilde balkonlara kurulan güneş enerjisi sistemlerine izin verilmesini istedi.
Çiler'in konuşmasından sonra birleşime ara veren Meclis Başkanvekili Pervin Buldan, aranın ardından komisyonun yerini almaması üzerine birleşimi, saat 14.00'te toplanmak üzere kapattı.

Liverpool, from big money individuals to the collective, are building formidable momentum. On a bitterly cold night in Belgium, Andoni Iraola’s team delivered an accomplished away display to bring Club Brugge’s impressive run to a halt and step closer to automatic qualification from the Champions League group.
A week that supposedly represented a test of Liverpool’s credentials has brought rich encouragement before Sunday’s Merseyside derby. Following the 4-0 destruction of Manchester United there was another display of outstanding finishing from Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz.
Isak took his tally for the season into double figures with a double while Wirtz scored for the third club game in succession to take the match away from a determined Brugge side. There was also another clean sheet, but this one was hard-earned against an opponent that had scored in every other game this season (18 matches in total) and won 10 of the previous 11 games.
Iraola said: “You see 3-0 and you can think it was an easy game but I don’t think it was. We were facing a very good team that was tied with us in the Champions League, having an incredible run of games and scoring loads of goals. I value a lot the clean sheet and the win.”
This was the first meeting between the clubs since Kenny Dalglish decided the European Cup final with an exquisite chip at Wembley in 1978. Their only other encounters were also in a European final – the two legged Uefa Cup final in 1976 that Liverpool won 4-3 on aggregate – when Brugge fans adopted You’ll Never Walk Alone as an anthem. Liverpool were made to feel at home as both sets of supporters joined in with a rendition before kick-off and Isak soon benefited from more Brugge hospitality.
The visitors were handed the initiative courtesy of a mistake from veteran goalkeeper Yann Sommer. The former Switzerland international was under no pressure when he misplaced a pass to Bradley Barcola. Barcola released Dominik Szoboszlai free inside the area and Liverpool’s captain for the night, with Virgil van Dijk rested on the bench, squared for Isak. The striker prodded the opener between the legs of the 37-year-old keeper.
Brugge were as energetic and aggressive in the press as Iraola had predicted, though Liverpool were both resilient and dangerous. There were more promising signs from Barcola as his sharpness and speed improves after a pre-season stalled by his move to Merseyside. Nicolò Tresoldi headed a corner from Félix Lemaréchal beyond Alisson but Szoboszlai was well placed to clear. Lemaréchal should have done better when found unmarked at the far post by the captain Hans Vanaken but steered a tame header straight at Alisson.
Liverpool endured an injury setback when Victor Muñoz collided into Jorne Spileers at the end of a surging run into the Brugge penalty area and caught his knee. “The worst part of the game,” said Iraola. “He was in a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was more positive after the game. A knock on the knee and we have to see how it presents itself.”
Muñoz’s replacement, Rio Ngumoha, did not take long to make his presence felt and continue the menacing form that helped dismantle United. Liverpool went close to a second goal when carving open the Brugge defence with a flowing, incisive move that deserved reward. Wirtz picked out Isak with a sweeping pass into the box. The striker cushioned his touch into the path of the incoming Szoboszlai and his first-time shot was destined for the far corner only for Sommer to redeem himself with a superb save.
Sommer’s save provided a platform for Brugge to enjoy a sustained spell of pressure, although Alisson was not seriously troubled until the 70th minute when he denied Lemaréchal with a fine stop at his near post.
Just as home hopes were growing, Liverpool extinguished them with a devastating counterattack from a loose Brugge ball on the edge of their area. Ngumoha led the charge, showing good strength to shrug off Carlos Forbs and then good awareness to find Wirtz unmarked. The German playmaker controlled on the edge of the box, gave Sommer the eyes, and swept home an excellent finish off the inside of the keeper’s right-hand post.
Minutes later Isak added to the showreel when racing clear on goal after Brandon Mechele slipped as the pair competed for Alisson’s quick clearance. The Sweden international advanced on Sommer’s goal and lifted an impudent chip over the keeper to cap a mature and clinical display from Iraola’s team.
“Alex is in a great moment right now,” the Liverpool head coach added. “In the first half especially he helped us a lot in the link up, we were finding him very easily. Sometimes they were leaving him one-v-one against the centre-backs and in one of those moments he has killed the game.”

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art:
Liverpool fans have needed to be patient to see the best of Alexander Isak after an injury-hit start to his career, but the striker is now proving the wait has been worth it.
By scoring twice against Club Brugge in the Champions League, Isak took his tally for the season to 10 - more than double his total for his first season at the Reds.
Of course, that campaign was disrupted; he had no pre-season because of his protracted £125m move from Newcastle and then suffered a broken leg in December.
But Isak is now in a hot streak of form, having scored four goals in his past four games for Liverpool.
Asked whether fans were now seeing his full capabilities, Isak told TNT Sports: "It is always difficult to say exactly where you are and how good you are but I can definitely say I feel good, I am in a good place and the team is in a good place which is the most important thing.
When Isak scored his opener against Club Brugge, it marked a sixth consecutive away game in which he has struck.
That meant he joined an exclusive club of just eight players to have achieved that feat, following in the footsteps of Dick Forshaw, Sam English, Gordon Hodgson, John Evans, John Aldridge, John Barnes and Mohamed Salah.
Isak has now scored the joint-most away goals across all competitions this season (eight – level with Erling Haaland).
His total is also already more than any Liverpool player managed away from home in the 2025-26 campaign (six by Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk) and it is only November.
Isak looks to be brimming with confidence, exemplified by his second goal as he latched on to a pass from Alisson to go through one-on-one and then chipped a confident finish past the goalkeeper.
But for Andoni Iraola, Isak's performance offered much more than goals, the Liverpool manager also praising the striker's overall contribution.
"In the first half especially he helped us with the link up. In the second half it was more about defending a little lower."
Alexander Isak scored twice against Club Brugge but also showed a willingness to drop back and help link up Liverpool's play
Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock agreed that Isak had shown he has more to his game than the goals.
"There were a lot of questions about Isak last year, about his price tag and what Liverpool paid for him," he said.
"There were a lot of people saying he doesn't take people on, but now he looks fitter and looks sharper and we are starting to see the quick, nimble feet again that we saw at Newcastle, with his nice touches and link-up play.
"So we are starting to see a different side of him. My big question in this system would be - can he press? Can he close down, can he affect the game in the other way that Iraola likes to do? Now we are starting to see that.
It is not just Isak who is looking the part in the Liverpool attack.
Florian Wirtz continued his impressive run of form with a goal that means he now has eight goal contributions in his last five games for Liverpool and Germany.
"Both are now in a good place," Iraola said of Wirtz and Isak.
"When the team overall is playing well and we are getting good results everything looks a little better.
"The important part if they help the team to play well and get results. Alex and Florian right now are in a good moment."
But the Liverpool attack as a whole is looking dangerous, regardless of who plays along with Isak and Wirtz.
In Wednesday's 3-0 win, it was Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola who completed the front four, while in Sunday's 4-0 defeat of Manchester United it was Rio Ngumoha who played in Munoz's position.
"We have so many good players in our team," Wirtz told TNT Sports.
"Even when we can substitute some wingers, midfielders or strikers in the 60th minute or later it gives us a lot.
"It shows how good our team is and it is important for a top team to have a strong bench."
Liverpool's win against Club Brugge was their seventh from their last 10 games across all competitions.
"I spoke to Wirtz at the weekend, after the [Manchester] United game, and we were talking about his form - and he said 'well it helps that the team are playing well'," Warnock added.
"It's true because if you try to influence a bad team or a team that's not playing well, then it is much harder.
"With a fitter Isak, Wirtz looks a better player because now he is playing balls in behind that Isak is getting to, and getting in on goal on the back of.
"It has a knock-on effect, which is obviously like Wirtz said, he is playing in a team which is better equipped to suit him."

Bayern Munich endured their first defeat of the season on Wednesday, losing 2-1 at Lille in the Champions League as a tough week for the German giants worsened.
Dayot Upamecano opened the scoring for Bayern but Ayase Ueda levelled for Lille before a horror Aleksandar Pavlovic own goal gifted the hosts victory. Bayern’s unbeaten record in all competitions was ended by a Lille side who kicked off in 35th place in the tournament’s league phase.
The defeat continued a diffiicult week for Bayern, who have lost star striker Harry Kane for several months to an ankle ligament injury on Friday and were also without Michael Olise due to a foot complaint. Teenage winger Lennart Karl was the only recognised forward in the visitors’ lineup, although Jamal Musiala and Luis Díaz came off the bench.
The centre-back Upamecano, a striker in his youth, had laughed off pre-game suggestions he could play up front. With 15 minutes gone, the Bayern defender channelled Kane when he rose highest to head in the opener from a Tom Bischof corner. Bayern controlled the first half, with little sign of the problems to come.
The visitors were fortunate when VAR intervened to disallow a Ueda goal early in the second half for a foul on Joshua Kimmich, but the Japan striker did get on the scoresheet after 62 minutes, guiding Nathan Ngoy’s diagonal pass into the bottom corner. Lille got the winner just four minutes later when Pavlovic chopped an Ethan Mbappé shot into his own goal in comical fashion.
Mbappé – the younger brother of Real Madrid striker Kylian – broke through on the counter and scuffed his shot against the post, only for Pavlovic to bundle the ball into his own net as he attempted to clear it away. “There are no excuses. It’s simply the reality we face, and we have to stand together,” Kompany said afterwards as the result left Bayern 15th in the table, facing a fight to avoid the playoffs.
Anthony Gordon scored twice as Barcelona cruised to a ⁠4-1 victory at Sabah , maintaining Hansi Flick’s ⁠side’s push for ⁠a ​top-eight finish with their fourth victory from five league-phase matches.
Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus ⁠also scored in the space of five second-half minutes for the Spanish champions, who are ⁠fourth in the 36-team league table, while the Azerbaijani debutants Sabah ​are 32nd.
Barcelona had been ‌frustrated for periods ‌in the first half before Adeyemi, filling in on ‌the right wing for the injured Lamine Yamal, delivered a cross that the goalkeeper, Stas Pokatilov, could only palm to the edge of the six-yard box and Gordon tapped home from close range.
Six minutes after the ‌restart, Pokatilov parried a Jesus effort straight into Gordon’s path and the England forward made no ​mistake. Adeyemi then scored himself in the 55th minute before Jesus added a fourth five minutes later. Sabah briefly lifted the crowd at ⁠the Baku Olympic Stadium when Joy-Lance Mickels found ​the net.
“I’ve been very successful here,” the England winger Gordon said after taking his goal tally in Baku to six goals in two appearances. “Two goals, I’m happy with that. A good performance, all in all, very good.”
Donyell Malen’s penalty earned Roma a 2-2 draw away to Paris Saint-Germain , ending the injury-hit champions’ perfect record in this season’s tournament.
Malen stroked in from the spot in the 78th minute at the Parc des Princes, giving Gian Piero Gasperini’s side a welcome point after their collapse from two goals up to lose 3-2 at Manchester United last time out.
Roma took an early lead through Mario Hermoso, only for Illia Zabarnyi to head home from a PSG corner before substitute Ousmane Dembélé briefly put the hosts in front with a penalty of his own. The result halts a run of 12 consecutive wins in all competitions for PSG, who sit second behind Real Madrid in the league table.
“It was the hardest match we have had this season and I am happy with the result,” said the PSG coach, Luis Enrique. “I hope we don’t have to play [Roma] later on over two legs.”
In Czechia, Villarreal earned their second win in five Champions League games thanks to Tajon Buchanan’s second-half winner against Slavia Prague . The Canada forward beat Jakub Markovic at his near post to secure a 1-0 win while the hosts were left to rue two major VAR interventions.
The Villarreal defender Renato Veiga was initially sent off for an elbow in the first half before it was downgraded to a yellow after a video review. Slavia had a late penalty overturned, too, after Pape Gueye’s challenge on Michal Sadilek was deemed not to be a foul after another look.
Elsewhere, Petar Sucic’s penalty set Internazionale on their way to a 2-0 home win over Stuttgart, Atlético Madrid saw off Norwegian side Viking by the same score, and Fenerbahce defeated nominal hosts Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0 at Stamford Bridge.

MÜZİK Yorumcuları Meslek Birliği (MÜYORBİR) üyeleri, sanatçı Ajda Pekkan 'ın 373 eserini kapsayan dijital telif davasında sanatçı lehine verilen kararı değerlendirdi. Nükhet Duru, "Bir sanatçının sesini, yorumunu, emeğini ona hakkını vermeden kullanmamalısınız" dedi. Sümer Ezgü, "Sanatçıların haklarını tek tek mahkemelerde aramadıkları, adil ve şeffaf bir sistem istiyoruz" diye konuştu. Onur Akın ise mahkemenin emsal teşkil edecek çok önemli bir karar verdiğini dile getirdi.
MÜYORBİR'in yaptığı açıklamada kararın icracı sanatçıların telif haklarının korunması açısından önemine dikkat çekildi. Birlik, sanatçıların hak edişlerinin şeffaf biçimde hesaplanması ve doğrudan kendilerine veya temsil edildikleri meslek birliklerine aktarılması çağrısını yineledi.
"Dijital müzik platformlarının henüz bulunmadığı 2001 yılı öncesinde plak, kaset veya CD formatında yayımlanmak üzere kaydedilen albümler, bugün çoğu zaman o eserleri seslendiren yorumcu sanatçıların izni alınmadan dijital müzik platformlarında yayımlanıyor. Fiziki formatlar için geçmişte verilen izinlerin, yıllar sonra ortaya çıkan dijital kullanımları da kapsadığı varsayılıyor.
26 yıllık köklü geçmişi ve 3 bine yakın yorumcu üyesiyle Türkiye'deki icracı sanatçıları temsil eden MÜYORBİR, 2001 öncesi kayıtların dijital kullanımına ilişkin telif hakları konusundaki mücadelesini uzun süredir sürdürüyor."
DURU: SANATÇININ YORUMUNU, EMEĞİNİ, HAKKINI VERMEDEN KULLANMAMALISINIZ
MÜYORBİR Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi, sanatçı Nükhet Duru da Ajda Pekkan kararının ardından tüm sanatçıların haklarının korunması gerektiğini belirterek, "Sevinçle öğrendik ki Ajda Pekkan da tüm davaları kazanmış. Benim de kazandığım davalar var. Bir sanatçının sesini, yorumunu, emeğini ona hakkını vermeden kullanmamalısınız. Bunu uzun süredir söylüyoruz. Türk yargı organları nihayet doğruyu görerek güzel kararlar veriyor. Müteşekkiriz. Hem bu emeği kullanmamalı hem de şeffaf biçimde hak edişlerini, bütün bir ömrünü sanatına ve halkına adayan sanatçıların hak edişlerini şeffaf bir şekilde takdim etmelisiniz" ifadelerini kullandı.
MÜYORBİR Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi, sanatçı Sümer Ezgü, şu açıklamayı yaptı:
"Tıpkı eski korsan kaset döneminde olduğu gibi bugün de dijital alanda sanatçıdan izinsiz yayınlar yapılıyor. Ayrıca sanatçılar, yapım şirketlerinden ne kadar dinlendikleri ya da izlendikleri konusunda şeffaf bilgiler alamıyor. YouTube, Spotify, Deezer gibi dijital platformlardan sanatçıların hakları ya aracısız olarak kendilerine ya da temsil edildikleri meslek birliklerine yatırılmalı. MÜYORBİR olarak sanatçıların haklarını tek tek mahkemelerde aramadıkları, adil ve şeffaf bir sistem istiyoruz. Nasıl ki bir fabrika işçisinin kol emeği varsa, sanatçının da sesi var, icrası var, yorumu var. Bu emeği ticari olarak kullanıyorsanız adil ve şeffaf olarak hakkını vermelisiniz"
MÜYORBİR Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi, sanatçı Onur Akın ise Ajda Pekkan kararının uzun yıllardır sürdürdükleri telif mücadelesi açısından önemine dikkat çekerek, "2001 öncesindeki bütün yayınlanmış eserlerin dijital hakları sanatçılara aittir, yapımcılara değil. Yapımcılar bu eserleri dijitalde izinsiz kullanamaz. Maalesef yıllardır izinsiz kullanılıyor. Sanatçılar haklarını aramaya başladılar ve yapımcılara karşı davalar açılmaya başlandı. Ben de dava açanlardan biriyim. Kazandığım ve şu an devam eden davalarım var. Mahkeme emsal teşkil edecek çok büyük bir karar verdi. Bundan sonra açılan davalar bu emsalle birlikte mutlaka sanatçıların lehine sonuçlanacaktır, yapımcılar haksız kazanç elde edemeyecek" dedi.

Two games, no wins. Two red cards, two goals scored. One goal disallowed, six conceded. Is it possible for Mauricio Pochettino to have learned anything from a crazy first week as Manchester United boss?
United and Pochettino went on the warpath before the Champions League encounter with Sporting, furious at Leny Yoro's dismissal at Liverpool which they believe was unjust and shaped the eventual 4-0 defeat.
Club officials were seething after the 2-2 draw in Lisbon as well.
This time it was 2022 World Cup final referee Szymon Marciniak in the firing line. Blowing before Amad's first-half header went into the net meant VAR had no chance to assess whether the Polish official was right to rule Youri Tielemans had fouled Goncalo Inacio before prodding the ball through to the Ivorian.
Former United winger Ashley Young didn't think so. He called Marciniak's performance "a disgrace".
That Tielemans picked up a booking that eventually led to his late red card – the Old Trafford outfit have now had four players sent off in their past five games, meaning the Belgian will miss the Old Trafford clash with RB Leipzig on 8 December - just compounded the situation.
Then, in a matter of minutes, Marciniak decided neither Manchester United keeper Senne Lammens nor Sporting counterpart Kaique had been fouled as they conceded. Their respective defences complained bitterly. Marciniak was only asked to go to the pitchside monitor by VAR for the latter incident, which he overturned.
United insiders felt the Tielemans incident was clearly not a foul and Amad's goal should have stood. They also felt any foul on Kaique by Patrick Dorgu was marginal and did not warrant their goal being disallowed.
Pochettino trod a fine path, knowing if he said something too controversial, it could land him with a fine.
A nod of a head in agreement was his initial reaction in his post-match news conference, when asked if he felt Marciniak had got it wrong.
A few minutes before, he was more expansive when he spoke to TNT.
"It's difficult to find a game where you get punished [so much] in one game," he said. "We were punished a lot in key actions."
Divots, howlers and bad decisions - dissecting Man Utd's draw in Lisbon
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino shows his frustration during the 2-2 draw with Sporting
Not for the first time this season, United controlled extended periods of a game they ended up not winning.
Seventy-five seconds after superbly saving one penalty, goalkeeper Lammens suffered a rush of blood and conceded another, which was scored.
Lammens was at fault for the second, when he dropped the ball into the path of Sporting striker Luis Suarez, who scored with an overhead kick.
"I think we dominated and we deserved to win the game, but we didn't for different circumstances," he said.
"All the teams make mistakes, but for these mistakes the punishment (for us) is too big in every single mistake. Many other clubs make mistakes or tilt in a different circumstance, in a more positive way. But that is in the way we are. We need to take responsibility."
United are still to win away from home in any competition this season. They have now won once in their last 13 matches. In the Champions League, they are 19th, two points in front of Roma, who are just below the top 24, which guarantees passage to the next phase.
Mauricio Pochettino asked about Amad's disallowed goal against Sporting
The Belgian's performance was not good and errors are beginning to mount.
It is not what Pochettino needs right now. United showed faith in the Belgium international this summer by bringing in 36-year-old Karl Darlow as his understudy.
Darlow did end last season as first choice at Leeds but started just 30 league games in his three seasons with the Elland Road club. Tom Heaton, 40, who was also on the bench against Sporting, has not played in a senior game since February 2023.
"This type of thing happens," he said. "That is football. Football is about making mistakes.
"I always want to support my player. I think we need to talk about responsibility. In this type of action our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult.
"It's not to blame the defensive line, but it's two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on. We need to manage his type of situation better."
Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens (left) and head coach Mauricio Pochettino applaud the away fans after the 2-2 draw at Sporting
It has been a whirlwind week for Pochettino, who last Wednesday morning UK time was still United States boss.
There have been a few blows to absorb, and lessons are having to be learned quickly.
But despite the clear frustrations, the 54-year-old is glad he accepted the challenge.
"I am happy to be here," he said. "I'm so excited to be the face representing this club.
"We are here because the situation wasn't the situation all the fans and people expect. We are here to take the responsibility from one week, and we are going to improve for sure.
"It's going to be tough, of course. Nothing is easy. But we have the energy and I think we have the capacity, and, most important, we have the players and the power and the energy from our fans, which is massive."

Report as Liverpool overpowered Club Brugge in Belgium with two goals from Alexander Isak and a fine strike from Florian Wirtz; Andoni Iraola's side rise to fifth in the Champions League phase standings, in prime position to finish inside the automatic qualifying spots
Liverpool recovered from their shock defeat to Fenerbahce in their last Champions League outing to beat Club Brugge 3-0 and improve their chances of a top-eight league phase finish.
Andoni Iraola's side have had no problem scoring goals in Europe, but faced issues keeping them out. Brugge were most obliging hosts in that respect, a far cry from the regularly free-scoring side that have so far averaged 2.75 goals per game and beaten Inter Milan at the San Siro.
Felix Lemarechal was the home side's greatest threat. But Alexander Isak was far more decisive, netting the opener following Yann Sommer's misplaced pass before rounding off the scoring in the second half with a deft chip to beat the goalkeeper. Sandwiched between was a superb strike from the in-form Florian Wirtz, set up by a surging run from Rio Ngumoha.
Brugge got better, Lemarechal twice forced Alisson into saves and Nicolo Tresoldi, who has scored the same number of Champions League goals as Erling Haaland this term, also called the Brazilian into action. But Liverpool were creatively superior. Momentum is building.
The only blemish of an otherwise perfect night for Andoni Iraola concerned an injury to Victor Munoz in the first half after clashing with Jorne Spileers. The coming together initially looked innocuous but the winger was unable to continue and immediately replaced by Rio Ngumoha. He walked off the pitch unaided despite the stretcher being called for.
Isak has now scored in six consecutive away outings for Liverpool while Wirtz continues to grow in stature and influence. The German has scored six times for club and country in the month of November alone. 12 points from five games gives the Reds a favourable chance of finishing inside the automatic qualifying positions, while Brugge drop to 13th - the first time they have tasted defeat in 11 games.
Florian Wirtz was, very briefly, the most expensive transfer in Premier League history when he joined Liverpool nearly 18 months ago. Only now is the German playmaker showing he was worth the record outlay.
His goal in Brugge marked a small but significant milestone, the first time he has scored in three consecutive appearances as a Liverpool player. It's been two years since the 23-year-old managed to find such consistency of output.
Wirtz's brilliance extended beyond his goal, linking play through the thirds and igniting attacks without relinquishing control out of possession. Finally, Iraola appears to have found a formula that brings the best out of the midfielder's qualities.
Here is a moment where the headline numbers have finally caught up with his growing influence.
"It was very positive. It puts us in a good position. We want to go to the top eight. We were efficient, a more difficult game than it looks now.
"It was difficult to expect a clean sheet, we expected an open game, man to man, so overall a very good performance. I appreciate a lot this win."
On Isak: "As a team, I value the first goal, but the second goal was also very nice."
"I feel good, I'm in a good place, the team is in a good place most importantly.
"That's where we want to be, and hopefully it just gets better from here."

Nottingham Forest’s manager, Oliver Glasner, believes standards at the club were not good enough prior to his arrival as he questioned why some of his squad cannot speak English after a number of years in the country.
Glasner was tempted to move to the City Ground by owner Evangelos Marinakis after winning the FA Cup and Conference League at Crystal Palace. However, Forest have won two of their opening 11 Premier League games and sit outside the relegation zone only on goal difference.
“Stability in a company is having standards,” said Glasner. “Everybody who joins commits to the standards. I think, very honestly, the standards were not high enough. We have players who are here for four years, [who] can’t speak English. If you go to Italy, after three months, every player gives his interview in the Italian language. For me, if I want to manage in England, I have to speak English.”
Glasner also revealed that he held talks with Marinakis in London on Monday in preparation for the January transfer window, when the club is targeting up to five signings.
“He [Marinakis] was asking ‘what do you need, what do you want here to improve in the squad, the staff and the environment’,” said Glasner. “He wants the best for Nottingham Forest, he wants the best for everyone here.
“We need to improve in the squad, in the staff, in the environment and this is our discussion. It was a fantastic meeting and it was worth spending six hours travelling.”
Forest are next in Premier League action on Friday when they host Chelsea.

Manchester United were held to a draw in a chaotic and controversial Champions League encounter with Sporting in Lisbon with Mauricio Pochettino denied a first win as United head coach despite his side turning around a first-half deficit.
They were behind at the break after goalkeeper Senne Lammens conceded from a penalty he gave away – having saved another just minutes before.
United then had a goal disallowed before scoring a penalty of their own through Bruno Fernandes, who then put them in front with the help of a large divot on the pitch.
Fernandes appeared to have inadvertently created the divot himself moments earlier when turning in the penalty area.
There was more drama as Lammens dropped the ball for Sporting's equaliser before Pochettino's side had what they thought was a winner ruled out.
Polish referee Szymon Marciniak was at the centre of much of the drama with midfielder Youri Tielemans sent off in stoppage time.
Lammens saved a poor penalty from Sporting's Luis Suarez, given after Lisandro Martinez left a leg out which caught Geny Catamo.
The Belgium keeper got down to hold on to Suarez's low effort which looked set to be a huge boost for the underperforming United number one.
Pochettino's whirlwind week ends with optimism and frustration
Lammens went from hero to zero in the space of 76 seconds as he rushed out of his goal and took out Maxi Araujo in the United box.
Noussair Mazraoui was caught out by a ball over the top but it was reckless from Lammens and this time Suarez buried the spot-kick.
Former United midfielder Owen Hargreaves told TNT Sports: "There is no way Senne Lammens can get there. Just stay in the goal."
Amad Diallo thought he had equalised for United before half-time when he headed in after his first attempted was turned on to the cross bar.
However, referee Marciniak blew his whistle for a foul against Youri Tielemans.
Replays showed Tielemans won the ball and pulled out of the challenge after he played the ball through to Amad.
BBC Sport's Dale Johnson: "Marciniak believed that Goncalo Inacio had been fouled by Youri Tielemens on the edge of the area as the Manchester United midfielder played a pass through.
"Rather than immediately blow his whistle, Marciniak held off to let the move play out.
"But when Diallo hit the bar with his first effort, Marciniak blew his whistle.
"Play was dead at that point, so when Diallo then nodded the rebound over the line the VAR was locked out.
"However, the chances that the VAR would have intervened were very slim.
"Tielemens, who was booked, caught Inacio's foot under his body sliding to make the pass, causing the Sporting defender's ankle to buckle."
Former Manchester United midfielder Ashley Young said on BBC Radio 5 Live: "It's an absolute disgrace. I don't know how the referee is seeing that Tielemans has kicked the player.
"On first viewing, I thought his foot must have hit him on the follow through but when you look at it again, Tielemans actually tries to take his foot away.
"He doesn't touch him because he knows the midfielder is coming towards him.
"It is one of the worst decisions I've seen with a referee giving that decision."
United got back on level terms after a foul on Martinez in the Sporting area by Eduardo Quaresma led to a penalty. Bruno Fernandes converted.
Former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha told BBC Sport: "Martinez wins that penalty, but it is a penalty."
United took the lead with two quick-fire goals but in bizarre circumstances as Fernandes' speculative strike looked like it would be easily collected by Kaique Pereira only to hit a divot on the pitch and fly up past the Sporting goalkeeper.
Former Rangers striker Ally McCoist on TNT Sports: "I think it hits a divot and it jumps over the goalkeeper! That is absolutely incredible."
Hargreaves added on TNT Sports: "Unbelievable. It is like a golf divot. There are holes in this pitch absolutely everywhere.
"Bruno Fernandes created a divot, does he get an assist for that?"
Lammens made another error, spilling a high ball under little pressure from Suarez. The Sporting striker then reacted quickly to find the target with an overhead kick to make it 2-2, the goal given after a quick VAR check.
McCoist: "I am baffled because the forward does what you expect him to do.
"The goalkeeper, instead of concentrating on the ball, he thinks about the player."
United thought they had taken the lead as Sporting keeper Kaique appeared to push the ball into his own net from a Fernandes corner.
However, after a VAR intervention, the 'goal' was then disallowed for a foul on the goalkeeper by Patrick Dorgu.
Onuoha: "First that was an absolutely disastrous goal for United to concede for the equaliser. it comes from a nothing ball into the box, too.
"For the United goal that has just been ruled out, the keeper has pushed it into his own net before Dorgu has touched him."
Young added on BBC Radio 5 Live: "The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me.
"If a referee is on the pitch and being sent to the screen, if he's given the goal then stand by your decision."
Midfielder Tielemans was then sent off for a late challenge on Sergi Altimira. The Belgium international's second yellow compounds the controversial one he received in the first half.
United have now received five red cards in all competitions this season - two more than any other Premier League side.
Young added: "The referee's performance was just simply 'wow'.
"The decisions that he gave. Youri Tielemans getting booked to eventually getting sent off later because you booked him when it should never have been a booking and it should have been an equalising goal.
"His decision-making today is nothing more than a disgrace."

There will also be a Champions League Match of the Day on BBC One on Wednesday, from 22:40 to 00:00.

Jamie Carragher felt Man Utd were 'unlucky' to be controversially denied two goals by refereeing decisions in their 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting and said Mauricio Pochettino will feel like his side were 'robbed' of what would have been a 'really big win'
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Jamie Carragher says Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens' confidence is a cause for concern after his howler cost Mauricio Pochettino a first win since taking charge.
It was a nightmare performance for Lammens, who unnecessarily conceded a penalty for Luis Suarez's opener just 75 seconds after saving the Sporting striker's poorly taken first spot-kick.
Lammens, 24, then spilt a routine cross late in the second half, allowing Suarez to equalise for 2-2 and denying United their first away win of the season and their first Champions League win on the road in five years.
The Belgium international, signed from Club Brugge in September 2025, restored calm between the sticks last season after Andre Onana's calamitous spell as No 1, but has had a poor start to his second year at Old Trafford.
Delivering his verdict on Lammens' performance, Carragher said on CBS : "You worry about the confidence of that goalkeeper now.
"That mistake for the equaliser, the 2-2 goal, you say sometimes 'an amateur goalkeeper wouldn't make that mistake'. If that was an amateur goalkeeper you'd be thinking 'that can't happen'. That just can't happen at this level."
Carragher questioned if United had the options in their goalkeeper department to bring Lammens out of the spotlight for a brief while.
Pochettino could call on Karl Darlow if he wanted to make a change at goalkeeper. He was signed in the summer on a free transfer from Leeds, where he was the No 1 for the second half of last season.
"It is getting to the stage with the goalkeeper now," Carragher added. "The focus on a Man Utd goalkeeper is always big if he's making mistakes. I don't think the back-up's even at the level where, no matter how poorly the goalkeeper plays, you change it."
Man Utd head coach Mauricio Pochettino backed Lammens and felt he needed help from his teammates.
Pochettino said: "That is football. Football is about making mistakes. I always want to support my players. It's something that happened in that case. I think we need to talk about responsibility and it's our responsibility too to provide the best tools.
"I think in this type of action, our defensive line also needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult. It's not to blame the defensive line, but it's two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on.
"Professional players need to refresh concepts, refresh details until that becomes a habit. And I think things that we need to improve are habits in a defensive way, offensive way, in all the areas.
"It's to blame us because I think we need to manage this type of situation better, because this situation, when you are a keeper, is not easy and you always need help from your teammates. But of course, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve the small details - for sure we will improve."
Carragher felt United were "unlucky" to see two goals controversially ruled out but criticised the players for allowing games to spiral out of control when they suffer set-backs.
The Sky Sports pundit said it must frustrate Pochettino but will make for an "unbelievable" watch when the fly-on-the-wall documentary being filmed this season is released.
"Why do they keep shooting themselves in the foot?" said Carragher. "As a manager, what can he really do about the goalkeeper or Tielemans making a stupid tackle at the end?
"He'll be really frustrated because that could have been a really big result for them tonight at 2-1, and there were unlucky with the 3-2 [goal being disallowed].
"He will feel they've been robbed by the referee and he'll say they should have won the game.
"But he'll be looking at isolated incidents and it feels like every game is mad. There's never a normal game where you win 1-0 or you draw 1-1 and nothing really happens. Something happens all the time that you're almost laughing at, or you've got your head in your hands if you're a Man Utd fan.
"There is always madness or craziness. I mean, the documentary is going to be unbelievable isn't it."
The last thing Pochettino needed after the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool - and Leny Yoro's now overturned red card - was more refereeing controversy. However, there was contention around both goals United had ruled out in Lisbon.
Amad had the ball in the back of the net toward the end of the first half to equalise - but not before the whistle had gone for what was judged to have been a foul by Tielemans, who clearly won the ball with his slide tackle.
The United midfielder received a booking for his follow-through on Sporting defender Inacio, who went down dramatically despite receiving the slightest of contact. VAR could not intervene as the whistle had gone.
Morrison, who said Tielemans "won the ball", was adamant that it was the wrong call.
United's second disallowed goal, which was ruled out following VAR intervention, saw Dorgu penalised for making contact with Sporting goalkeeper Kaique before he punched into his own net.
Carragher felt it was "very harsh" for the referee to disallow the goal after being sent to his monitor.

Mauricio Pochettino was denied a first victory as Manchester United head coach by a goalkeeping howler from Senne Lammens in an incident-packed 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League as Youri Tielemans was sent off late on.
United looked to be on course for a first away win of the season after captain Bruno Fernandes scored two goals in the first five minutes of the second half - the second courtesy of a divot on the pitch - only for Lammens to spill the ball in the box for Luis Suarez to equalise with his second goal of the game.
Pochettino thought United had gone back in front for a second time shortly after Lammens' error when Sporting goalkeeper Kaique punched into his own net at a corner. However, it was ruled out following an on-field review for a foul by substitute Patrick Dorgu.
United were also aggrieved by a decision to rule out a goal by Amad before the break for an alleged foul by Tielemans that resulted in the first of his two bookings. Sky Sports' Dan Khan described the decision as "genuinely one of the worst decisions I've seen live."
It was a damaging night for Lammens, who gave away the penalty for Suarez's first goal just 75 seconds after saving the Sporting striker's poorly taken spot-kick. The man brought in to replace the error-prone Andre Onana is now beginning to resemble his predecessor.
Fernandes' equaliser three minutes after the restart came from the third penalty of what was a bizarre match. Few moments topped the United skipper's freakish second goal which came thanks to a tame effort bouncing up off a divot in the ground and into the back of the net.
Tielemans' stoppage-time red will only add to United's frustrations. It was his first booking, for a tame follow-through on Goncalo Inacio, that denied Amad Diallo from equalising late in the first half in one of the more baffling refereeing decisions you will see.
Pochettino's first two matches have seen his side have two players sent off and concede two penalties. If he did not know it before, he certainly knows now that nothing comes easy at United, who sit 19th in the Champions League and Premier League.
The last thing Pochettino needed after the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool - and Leny Yoro's now overturned red card - was more refereeing controversy. However, there was contention around both goals United had ruled out in Lisbon.
Amad had the ball in the back of the net toward the end of the first half to equalise - but not before the whistle had gone for what was judged to have been a foul by Tielemans, who clearly won the ball with his slide tackle.
The United midfielder received a booking for his follow through on Sporting defender Inacio, who went down dramatically despite receiving the slightest of contact. VAR could not intervene as the whistle had gone.
"It is a terrible decision," said Sky Sports pundit Clinton Morrison. "Tielemans won the ball."
United's second disallowed goal, which was ruled out following VAR intervention, saw Dorgu penalised for making contact with Sporting goalkeeper Kaique before he punched into his own net.
Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher felt it was "very harsh" for the referee to disallow the goal after being sent to his monitor.
"I do think United were a little bit unlucky tonight with the goal disallowed just before half-time. The goal at the end felt very harsh to me, the one where it could have been 3-2...

"That mistake for the equaliser, the 2-2 goal, you say sometimes 'an amateur goalkeeper wouldn't make that mistake' and that just can't happen at this level."
"I'm so proud of the players. It was a tough game. I liked the team we played for 90 minutes, the personality, the character. It's difficult to find a game where you get punished in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions. Today we showed how we want to play after just one week of working together.
"We need to concentrate and focus more, try to recover better. The performance like today's is the best medicine to prepare for the next game."
On Lammens' mistake for equaliser: "That is football. Football is about making mistakes. I always want to support my players. It's something that happened in that case. I think we need to talk about responsibility and it's our responsibility too to provide the best tools.
"I think in this type of action, our defensive line also needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult. It's not to blame the defensive line, but it's two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on.
"Professional players need to refresh concepts, refresh details until that becomes a habit. And I think things that we need to improve are habits in a defensive way, offensive way, in all the areas.
"It's to blame us because I think we need to manage this type of situation better, because this situation, when you are a keeper, is not easy and you always need help from your teammates. But of course, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve the small details - for sure we will improve."

George Hirst scored both goals as Stoke secured a fifth successive Championship win by beating Millwall 2-1 to go level on points with Middlesbrough at the top.
The Scotland international scored his second goal for the Potters in the 1-0 win over Birmingham on Saturday and doubled his tally for the season to take Stoke back into the automatic promotion places.
Mark Sykes’s stunning strike halved the deficit in the final 10 minutes, but Stoke held on to claim an 11th win in their past 14 outings. The defeat was Millwall’s fourth in a row, coming a day after it was announced they had been ordered to play a future match in front of a partially closed stadium for offensive chanting.
“There’s been a little bit said about George that is unfair,” said the Stoke manager, Mark Robins. “It’s amazing if you just remember that you love playing football and you just go and do it, everything else tends to fall into place. It’s not as simple as that but it really helps, and he’s done that.”
Burnley set a new record for the longest home run without a league win as Birmingham reaffirmed their promotion credentials with a 2-0 victory at Turf Moor thanks to August Priske’s strike and Jaydon Banel’s own goal.
It is now 24 games since Burnley last earned three points in front of their own fans, a nightmare run that has now stretched to 403 days. It represents the worst sequence in the history of English football.
Burnley, relegated from the Premier League last season, remain in the drop zone, one point above the bottom side Derby. Fabio Celestini has picked up three points in the five games he has taken charge of since succeeding Nicky Hayen last month and his team were jeered off at the end. For Birmingham, it was a timely return to form after a 1-0 defeat at Stoke. Chris Davies’s team are two places and two points off the automatic promotion spots.
Watford ’s new head coach, Edward Iordanescu, watched from the stands as Todd Cantwell’s penalty condemned the struggling hosts to a 1-0 defeat by resilient Blackburn . The former Romania national team manager, who had just flown in after signing a contract, was introduced to a sparsely populated Vicarage Road to polite applause, 10 minutes before kick-off.
On the evidence of Watford’s third home defeat of the season, he will have his work cut out to steer them away from the Championship’s relegation quicksands.
The Norwegian duo Aune Heggebø and Felix Horn Myhre scored the goals as West Brom boosted their promotion push with a 3-1 win at Bolton . Heggebø gave James Morrison’s in-form visitors the lead which was cancelled out by Ruben Rodrigues’s second-half penalty.
But West Brom, without their injured top scorer Isaac Price, finished strongly, with Myhre’s fifth goal since his summer move from Brann restoring West Brom’s lead after 75 minutes. Heggebø, back in the starting lineup after Saturday’s draw with Swansea, sealed a fifth win in eight games with a penalty.
“I thought [Heggebø] would be perfect for this game if we could get behind their high back line,” said Morrison. On Price’s absence, the West Brom manager added: “Any team would miss big players and what they bring to the team. But it’s not to cry about, it is about trying to find the best way and trust in the players who come in.”

Crystal Palace’s influential supporters’ group disbanded 24 hours before their first home game this season – and Selhurst Park has not been the same since
S imon Teesdale could not help feeling mixed emotions when his beloved Crystal Palace won the Conference League in Leipzig in May. He started going to Selhurst Park with his father in the 1980s, became a season-ticket holder in the 1990s and has watched with pride as the club established itself as a permanent fixture in the Premier League over the past 14 years. Palace finally secured a major trophy in the 2025 FA Cup final – an experience Teesdale remembers as “one of the best days of my life” – and followed that up by winning the Conference League but he decided in August not to renew his season ticket.
“Something happened between the FA Cup win and today that changed me,” he wrote in an emotional article published last month on his website. “Tipped me over the edge. Actually, it’s fairer to say that something accelerated in that period of time. The seeds were sown years ago.”
Teesdale details how the matchday experience at Palace – bottom of the Premier League for the first time since 2017 after five straight defeats – has been transformed by “fireworks, light shows and excessively loud music at key moments before, during and after the match”. He likens it to listening to Natasha Bedingfield’s Unwritten – one of the most unpopular songs on the Palace playlist – on a loop. “A song about writing your own story, that’s played on matchdays to drown us out as we attempt to write ours.”
“As a fan of another team, people will be thinking: ‘What on earth are you moaning about?’” Teesdale says. “But it’s harder to put your emotions and your experience of what it’s like to commit to being a fan into words that are beyond just what you see on paper, like winning trophies and whatever else. If I had to tie it down to one thing, it was the perception that the club was losing its identity. It just seemed that no one was really being thought about as a genuine Palace fan any more.”
Teesdale’s decision to give up his season ticket happened to coincide with the news that Palace’s influential supporters’ group the Holmesdale Fanatics (HF) was disbanding 24 hours before their first home game of the season against Manchester City.
In February, it had criticised the club’s attempts “to keep trying to force an ‘American-style experience’ on us” after asking for the music to be turned off during the warm-up, only for that request to be refused by Palace’s chief executive, Sharon Lacey, blaming Uefa regulations. The HF claimed another request to turn off the music before a Premier League game against Leeds a few weeks later was rejected because the club had a “production plan” in place for matches.
The HF’s statement in August cited “never-ending problems with the club right up to the present day” as one of the reasons for its sudden disappearance from its traditional home behind the goal in Block E of the Holmesdale Road Stand. “Attempts to sanitise the game are stronger than ever,” it wrote.
The HF’s absence has been felt significantly at Selhurst Park. Pierre Sage said early in his doomed 16-game spell as manager that the unique atmosphere it created at home and on the way to the Conference League final against Rayo Vallecano had played a part in convincing him to succeed Oliver Glasner. “We are waiting for them, I expect they will come back quickly,” he said in September after the 4-0 win over Lech Poznan.
The Palace chair, Steve Parish, defended the pre-match playlist and told the Athletic in an interview a week later that he was disappointed by the HF’s decision to disband but remained confident that “something exciting will grow out of it”. Teesdale was also contacted by Lacey after his article was published last month and she told him that she expected them back, “in a slightly different format”, in Block E soon. When approached by the Guardian, a former member of the HF did not want to comment and referred to its August statement announcing it would end all organised stadium activity at Selhurst Park after 20 years.
A defamation claim lodged in the high court by the Nottingham Forest owner, Evangelos Marinakis, 16 days before the announcement the HF was disbanding could be another explanation for their continued absence.
It was made a fortnight before the one-year limitation period was due to expire against Palace’s owners, CPFC Limited, and “Persons Unknown” in response to the incendiary banner held up in the Holmesdale Road End during Palace’s game against Forest in August 2025 . Marinakis says that it made a number of serious allegations about him and depicted him holding a gun to the head of the England midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White. The case is due to be heard in the coming months, with Marinakis and CPFC Limited having instructed prominent solicitors and “Persons Unknown” to be represented by “litigant in person”, ie themselves.
Palace were fined £50,000 by the Football Association after being found guilty of failing “to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters or followers) didn’t behave in an improper, offensive, abusive, insulting and/or provocative way at this match”. The FA added in its statement in February: “The fact that Crystal Palace had a policy to prevent banners being smuggled into the stadium demonstrates that it was aware of the risk.”
Parish and Lacey have said publicly they did not know exactly why the HF – whose motto was “this mentality is unstoppable” – disbanded and there was no mention of the banner on its statement. Yet it seems extremely likely there is a connection.
Teesdale says he was surprised to receive a call from Lacey but believes the only female chief executive in the Premier League has Palace’s best interests at heart. Teesdale is still deciding whether to attend.
“I’ve been twice this season,” he wrote in his article. “Both times in Block E. Surrounded by the ghost of the HF. The whole experience was strangely dispassionate. I was verging on bored. No drum. Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Burnley and Birmingham City at Turf Moor on Wednesday night; Clarets make it 24 winless games in a row at home in the league, the longest run in English Football League history.
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Burnley set a new record for the longest home run without a league win as Birmingham reaffirmed their Sky Bet Championship promotion credentials with a 2-0 victory at Turf Moor thanks to August Priske's strike and Jaydon Banel's own goal.
It is now 24 games since the Clarets last celebrated three points in front of their own fans, a nightmare run that has now stretched to 403 days. It represents the worst sequence in the history of English football.
Burnley, relegated from the Premier League last season, remain firmly ensconced in the drop zone. Coach Fabio Celestini has picked up just three points in the five games he has taken charge off since succeeding Nicky Hayen last month and his team were jeered off at the end.
For City, however, it was a timely return to form following the 1-0 defeat at Stoke on Saturday. This was a seventh win in nine for Chris Davies' team and they are just two places and two points off the automatic promotion spots.
Burnley started on the front foot, with Aaron Ramsey forcing goalkeeper James Beadle into action with a low drive from 25 yards.
But the visitors went ahead in the seventh minute when James Stansfield was found in space by Carlos Vicente and his driven cross was diverted home by the sliding Priske. It was the Dane's eighth goal of the season.
The Clarets responded positively, with Largie Ramazani forcing Beadle into two smart saves and also having a shot deflected over. Zeki Amdouni also sent a decent chance too high.
Watford 0-1 Blackburn: Todd Cantwell penalty steers Rovers to victory

Charlton Athletic 4-0 Lincoln City: Addicks sweep to victory at The Valley
Birmingham should have doubled their lead just before the break, but after Liam Millar had shaken off a couple of weak challenges, his shot lacked pace and precision and home keeper Max Weiss was able to save.
The visitors doubled their lead in the 52nd minute when Millar's inswinging corner from the right flicked off Banel's head and looped into the far corner of his own goal.
Priske saw the ball shave the post as he arrived under pressure from Max Alleyne to meet Bright Osayi-Samuel's cross as the visitors looked to turn the screw, with Burnley's fans beginning to voice their discontent.
The Clarets' only win this season came at Watford last month. They have now conceded 35 goals, the same number as bottom club Derby.
It needed a sprawling Weiss save to prevent defender Igor scoring the second own goal of the game when he sent an attempted chest pass towards the corner of the net before the keeper intervened.
Celestini sent on Jamie Vardy in an attempt to salvage something, only for fellow substitute Andreas Hountondji to see his shot saved by Beadle after breaking clear.
Birmingham could have scored again four minutes from time but Demarai Gray's penalty was saved by Weiss after he had been fouled by Alleyne.
"I understand the fans are frustrated. They have been waiting for a victory here for a long time. The reaction the fans showed is right at this moment, so it is head down and work harder.
"If they see some good things then they are with us 100 per cent, like they were at the start. They are frustrated but we have to change that.
"We lost the game because Birmingham were better than us in both boxes. In the 70 metres in the centre of the pitch, we were better than them. But they have one shot and score one goal and that made it very difficult.
"If we can be more efficient then I will be in absolutely no doubt about my team because I see good things. Tomorrow is another day and we must keep fighting.

"It was an excellent win. It was all about solidity, appetite and application.
"I am told this was our fifth away win, which was as many as we managed in the whole of last season, so that shows you something.
"I made a few changes and I think the balance I was trying to strike came to fruition. We scored twice and could have scored even more. We created some very good chances.
"I heard some of our fans had a problem on the M6. It took some of them three hours to get here on a freezing midweek night in the middle of winter.
"So it was good to play like that, get the win and send them home loud and proud and happy with their team."

Türk öğrencilerin Avrupa'daki eğitim fırsatlarına erişimini zorlaştıran Schengen vizesi sorunu için Türkiye'nin girişimiyle Schengen ülkelerinin Türkiye'deki temsilcilikleri arasında özel bir çalışma grubu kuruldu. Passport Reports'un hesabına göre Schengen ülkeleri Türk vatandaşlarına vize muafiyeti tanırsa vizesiz gidilebilen ülke sayısı 69'dan 98'e, Türk pasaportunun dünya sıralaması ise 74'ten 39'a yükselecek.
Schengen vizesi için randevu almakta zorlanan öğrenciler, vize süreçleri uzadığı için Avrupa'daki eğitim programlarını kaçırma tehlikesiyle yüzleşiyor. Mağduriyetin giderilmesi için Türkiye'nin girişimiyle Schengen ülkelerinin Türkiye'deki temsilcilikleri arasında özel bir çalışma grubu oluşturuldu.
Grubun, Ankara 'da yapılan Yerel Schengen İşbirliği toplantısının ardından kurulduğu aktarıldı. Türkiye'nin masaya taşıdığı taleplerin başında randevu süreçlerinin kolaylaştırılması, başvuruların daha kısa sürede sonuçlanması, istenen belgelerin azaltılması ve çok girişli, uzun süreli vizelerin yaygınlaştırılması geliyor.
Türkiye, 29 Schengen ülkesinin vatandaşlarına vizesiz seyahat imkânı tanıyor. Bu ülkelerden 16'sının vatandaşları sınırdan pasaporta bile gerek duymadan, sadece kimlik kartıyla içeri girebiliyor.
Türk vatandaşları için tablo tersine dönüyor: Schengen bölgesinin tamamına seyahat etmek için vize almak zorundalar. Karşılıklılık dengesinin bu kadar bozuk göründüğü başka bir bölge Türk pasaportu için pek bulunmuyor.
Passport Reports'un 23 Kasım 2026 tarihli verilerine göre Türkiye pasaport sıralamasında 74. basamakta yer alıyor. Türk pasaportunun gerisinde kalan birçok ülkenin vatandaşı ise Schengen'e vizesiz girebiliyor.
Sıralamada Arnavutluk 75., Nikaragua 76., Venezuela 77., Mikronezya 79., Palau 80., Doğu Timor 85. ve Kosova 91. sırada bulunuyor. Yani Schengen kapısı, Türkiye'nin aşağısındaki bu ülkelerin pasaportlarına açık; Türk pasaportuna ise vizeyle açılıyor.
Mevcut tabloda Türk vatandaşları 69 ülkeye doğrudan vizesiz giriş yapabiliyor. Otuz ülkede kapıda vize , yedi ülkede ise elektronik seyahat izni yeterli oluyor.
Geriye kalan 92 ülke için ise seyahatten önce vize başvurusu yapmak şart. Schengen bölgesi de bu listenin en kalabalık ve en çok başvuru yapılan kısmını oluşturuyor.
Passport Reports'un hesaplamasına göre 29 Schengen ülkesi Türk vatandaşlarına vize muafiyeti tanıdığı anda vizesiz gidilebilen ülke sayısı 69'dan 98'e fırlayacak. Türk pasaportu da 74. sıradan 39. sıraya yükselerek tam 35 basamak atlayacak.
Çalışma grubunun görevi şimdilik vize uygulamalarını gözden geçirmek ve başvuru süreçlerini sadeleştirmek. Muafiyetin kendisi bu grubun gündeminde değil; Türkiye ise Vize Serbestisi Diyaloğu'nun tamamlanmasını öncelikli hedef olarak tutuyor ve Dışişleri Bakanı Hakan Fidan'ın daha önce açıkladığına göre tamamlanması gereken 6 kriter kaldı.

Amerikan Basketbol Ligi (NBA) Kupası'nda Houston Rockets, konuk ettiği Phoenix Suns'ı 116-104 yenerken milli oyuncu Alperen Şengün de yaptığı " triple-double "la galibiyete katkı verdi. Peki, Triple-double nedir? Basketbolda Triple-double ne demek?
İngilizcede kabaca "üçlü çift" anlamına gelen terim, üç ayrı istatistikte çift haneli rakamı anlatıyor. En sık görülen biçimi sayı, ribaunt ve asist üçlüsü. Bir oyuncu maçı 10 sayı, 10 ribaunt ve 10 asistle bitirirse sınırı tam olarak geçmiş olur. 40 sayı atıp 10 ribaunt alan ama 9 asistte kalan oyuncu ise triple-double yapmış sayılmaz. Top çalma ve blokta 10'a ulaşmak çok seyrek görüldüğü için bu iki kategori hesaba nadiren girer.
Double-double, aynı beş kategoriden ikisinde 10 ve üstü rakamdır. Pivotlar için 20 sayı ve 12 ribauntluk bir maç bu yüzden sık rastlanan bir double-double. Quadruple-double ise dört kategoride çift hane demek ve NBA'de resmî olarak yalnız dört kez görüldü: Nate Thurmond (1974), Alvin Robertson (1986), Hakeem Olajuwon (1990) ve David Robinson (1994).
Ligin kariyer rekoru Russell Westbrook'ta. Westbrook, Mayıs 2021'de Oscar Robertson'ın 181 triple-double'lık rekorunu geçmişti. Robertson 1961-62 sezonunu maç başına triple-double ortalamasıyla bitiren ilk oyuncuydu; aynı ortalamayı Westbrook dört sezon tutturdu.

Türk vatandaşlarının Schengen vizesi başvurularında yaşadığı sorunlar sürerken, özellikle Avrupa'da eğitim almak isteyen öğrencilerin mağduriyetlerinin giderilmesi için harekete geçildi.
Türkiye'nin girişimiyle Schengen ülkelerinin Türkiye'deki diplomatik temsilcilikleri arasında özel çalışma grubu oluşturuldu.
Türkiye Gazetesi'nin haberine göre, vize randevusu bulmakta güçlük çeken ve uzun başvuru süreçleri nedeniyle eğitim programlarını kaçırma riski yaşayan öğrencilerin sorunları için yeni bir çalışma başlatıldı.
Türkiye'nin girişimiyle kurulan özel çalışma grubunda, Schengen ülkelerinin Türkiye'deki diplomatik temsilcilikleri yer alıyor. Çalışmayla öğrencilerin vize süreçlerinde karşılaştığı sorunlara çözüm bulunması hedefleniyor.
Türkiye, Schengen Bölgesi'ne üye 29 ülkenin vatandaşlarına vizesiz seyahat imkânı sunuyor. Bu ülkelerden 16'sının vatandaşları Türkiye'ye yalnızca kimlik kartlarıyla giriş yapabiliyor.
Buna karşılık bordo pasaport sahibi Türk vatandaşlarının Schengen ülkelerine seyahat edebilmek için vize alması gerekiyor.
Passport Reports'un 23 Kasım 2026 tarihli verilerine göre Türkiye, dünya pasaport sıralamasında 74'üncü basamakta bulunuyor.
Türkiye'nin gerisinde yer alan Arnavutluk, Nikaragua, Venezuela, Mikronezya, Palau, Doğu Timor ve Kosova vatandaşlarının Schengen Bölgesi'ne vizesiz seyahat edebilmesi dikkat çekiyor.
Mevcut durumda Türk vatandaşları 69 ülkeye vizesiz, 30 ülkeye kapıda vizeyle, 7 ülkeye ise elektronik seyahat izniyle giriş yapabiliyor. Önceden vize alınması gereken ülke sayısı ise 92.
Passport Reports'un hesaplamasına göre Schengen ülkelerinin Türk vatandaşlarına vize muafiyeti tanıması halinde doğrudan vizesiz seyahat edilebilen ülke sayısı 69'dan 98'e çıkabilecek.
Bu düzenlemenin hayata geçirilmesi durumunda Türk pasaportunun dünya sıralamasında 35 basamak yükselerek 74'üncü sıradan 39'uncu sıraya çıkabileceği öngörülüyor.
